translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 282.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 282.

sentences.zh: 【後晉紀三】起屠維大淵獻，盡重光赤奮若，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Later Jin Annals 3] From Tuyi Dayuanxian through Chongguang Chifenruo—three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Jin Annals 3] From the year jihai through the year xinmao—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝中天福四年（

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, the Sagely, Literary, Martial, Bright, Virtuous, and Filial, in the fourth year of Tianfu of the Middle Kingdom (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu, the Sagely, Literary, Martial, Bright, Virtuous, and Filial, in the fourth year of Tianfu (

sentences.zh: 己亥，公元九三九年）

translations.literal: jihai, corresponding to 939 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jihai, corresponding to 939 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛亥，以澶州防禦使太原張從恩為樞密副使。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinhai, Zhang Cong'en of Taiyuan, Military Commissioner of Defense at Dazhou, was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month's xinhai day, Zhang Cong'en of Taiyuan, defender of Dazhou, was made vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度使張希崇卒，羌胡寇鈔，無復畏憚。

translations.literal: Zhang Xichong, Military Commissioner of Shuofang, died; Qiang and Hu raided and plundered, no longer fearing restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xichong, military commissioner of Shuofang, died, and Qiang and Hu bands raided the borders without fear.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以義成節度使馮暉為朔方節度使。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, Feng Hui, Military Commissioner of Yicheng, was appointed Military Commissioner of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day, Feng Hui, military commissioner of Yicheng, was appointed military commissioner of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 党項酋長拓跋彥超最為強大，暉至，彥超入賀，暉厚遇之，因為於城中治第，豐其服玩，留之不遣，封內遂安。

translations.literal: Among the Tangut chieftains, Toba Yanchao was the most powerful. When Hui arrived, Yanchao came in to congratulate him; Hui treated him generously, had a mansion built for him in the city, lavished him with fine robes and ornaments, and detained him without sending him away—and the circuit was thereafter at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Tangut chiefs, Toba Yanchao was the strongest. When Feng Hui took up his post, Yanchao came to offer congratulations; Hui received him warmly, built him a residence in the city, showered him with fine dress and curios, and kept him there without letting him leave—and the region was soon quiet.

sentences.zh: 唐群臣江王知證等累表請唐主複姓李，立唐宗廟，乙丑，唐主許之。

translations.literal: The Tang ministers, including Prince Jiang Xu Zhizheng and others, repeatedly memorialized asking the Tang ruler to restore the surname Li and establish the Tang ancestral temple; on the day yichou, the Tang ruler granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Tang ministers led by Prince Jiang Xu Zhizheng repeatedly petitioned the Tang ruler to resume the Li surname and erect a Tang ancestral temple; on yichou day he consented.

sentences.zh: 群臣又請上尊號，唐主曰：「尊號虛美，且非古。」

translations.literal: The ministers again asked that he accept an honorific title; the Tang ruler said, "Honorific titles are empty flattery and are not ancient custom."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers again urged an honorific title upon him; the Tang ruler replied, "Such titles are hollow praise and are not the ancient way."

sentences.zh: 遂不受。

translations.literal: He therefore did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore declined.

sentences.zh: 其後子孫皆踵其法，不受尊號，又不以外戚輔政，宦者不得預事，皆他國所不及也。

translations.literal: Thereafter his descendants all followed his practice: they did not accept honorific titles, did not let maternal relatives assist in government, and did not allow eunuchs to take part in affairs—things unmatched by other states.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants thereafter followed his example: they refused honorific titles, kept maternal kin from governing, and barred eunuchs from state affairs—practices other realms could not match.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙亥，改太祖廟號曰義祖。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day yihai, the temple name of the founding ancestor was changed to Yizu (Ancestor of Righteousness).
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yihai day, the founding ancestor's temple name was changed to Yizu.

sentences.zh: 己卯，唐主為李氏考妣發哀，與皇后斬衰居廬，如初喪禮，朝夕臨凡五十四日。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, the Tang ruler began mourning for his Li forebears; he and the empress wore the severest hemp and dwelt in the mourning hut, observing the rites of the first days of bereavement, attending morning and evening for fifty-four days in all.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day the Tang ruler entered mourning for his Li forebears; he and the empress wore full mourning garb and lived in the mourning hut as at the start of bereavement, attending the bier morning and evening for fifty-four days.

sentences.zh: 江王知證、饒王知諤請亦服斬衰；

translations.literal: Prince Jiang Xu Zhizheng and Prince Rao Xu Zhi'e asked to wear the severest hemp as well;
translations.idiomatic: Princes Jiang Xu Zhizheng and Rao Xu Zhi'e asked to wear full mourning as well;

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: they were refused.

sentences.zh: 李建勳之妻廣德長公主假衰絰，入哭盡哀，如父母之喪。

translations.literal: Li Jianxun's wife, the Princess of Guangde, wore mourning dress and entered to weep with full grief, as for the death of parents.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jianxun's wife, the Princess of Guangde, donned mourning dress, entered, and wept with the grief due to parents.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，詔國事委齊王璟詳決，惟軍旅以聞。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, an edict entrusted state affairs to Prince Qi Jing for detailed decision, reporting only military matters.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day an edict delegated civil affairs to Prince Qi Jing for final decision, reserving military matters for direct report.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，唐主更名昪。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, the Tang ruler changed his name to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day the Tang ruler took the name Bian.

sentences.zh: 詔百官議二祚合享禮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the officials to deliberate on the rites for joint offerings to the two founding lines.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the officials to debate the rites for joint ancestral offerings to the two lines.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，宋齊丘等議以義祖居七室之東。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Song Qiqiu and others proposed placing Yizu in the eastern side of the seven chambers.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day Song Qiqiu and others proposed placing Yizu in the eastern bay of the seven ancestral chambers.

sentences.zh: 唐主命居高祖於西室，太宗次之，義祖又次之，皆為不祧之主。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler ordered that Gaozu occupy the western chamber, Taizong next, and Yizu after that—all as undeparted ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler ordered Gaozu placed in the western chamber, Taizong next, and Yizu after him—all as permanent, undeparted ancestors.

sentences.zh: 群臣言：「義祖諸侯，不宜與高祖、太宗同享，請於太廟正殿後別建廟祀之。」

translations.literal: The ministers said, "Yizu was a feudal lord and should not share offerings with Gaozu and Taizong; we ask that a separate temple be built behind the main hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple to worship him."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers argued, "Yizu was only a feudal lord and ought not share the altar with Gaozu and Taizong; let a separate shrine be built behind the main hall to receive his cult."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾自幼托身義祖，向非義祖有功於吳，朕安能啟此中興之業？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "From childhood I was entrusted to Yizu; had Yizu not rendered great service to Wu, how could I have begun this work of restoration?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "I was raised under Yizu from childhood; without his great service to Wu, how could I have launched this restoration?"

sentences.zh: 群臣乃不敢言。

translations.literal: The ministers then dared not speak further.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers fell silent.

sentences.zh: 唐主欲祖吳王恪，或曰：「恪誅死，不若祖鄭王無懿。」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler wished to take Prince Wu Ke as ancestor; someone said, "Ke was executed—better to take Prince Zheng Wu Yi."
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler wished to trace descent from Prince Wu Li Ke; some said, "Ke died by execution—it would be better to take Prince Zheng Wu Yi."

sentences.zh: 唐主命有司考二王苗裔，以吳王孫禕有功，禕子峴為宰相，遂祖吳王，雲自峴五世至父榮。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler ordered the authorities to examine the descendants of the two princes; because Prince Wu's grandson Li Yi had merit and Yi's son Li Xian had been chief minister, he took Prince Wu as ancestor, declaring the line from Xian five generations to his father Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler ordered officials to trace both lines; because Prince Wu's grandson Li Yi had rendered service and Yi's son Li Xian had served as chief minister, he took Prince Wu as ancestor, declaring descent from Xian five generations down to his father Rong.

sentences.zh: 其名率皆有司所撰。

translations.literal: Those names were all composed by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Those names were all supplied by the court genealogists.

sentences.zh: 唐主又以歷十九帝、三百年，疑十世太少。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler also noted that the Tang had passed through nineteen emperors and three hundred years, and doubted that ten generations were too few.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler also reflected that the Tang had known nineteen emperors over three hundred years and wondered whether ten generations were too few.

sentences.zh: 有司曰：「三十年為世，陛下生於文德，已五十年矣。」

translations.literal: The authorities said, "Thirty years make a generation; Your Majesty was born in the Wende reign and is already fifty years old."
translations.idiomatic: The authorities replied, "Thirty years count as one generation; Your Majesty was born in the Wende era and is already fifty."

sentences.zh: 遂從之。

translations.literal: He therefore followed their view.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted their reasoning.

sentences.zh: 盧損至福州，閩主稱疾不見，命弟繼恭主之。

translations.literal: Lu Sun arrived at Fuzhou; the Min ruler claimed illness and did not receive him, ordering his younger brother Jigong to preside in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Sun reached Fuzhou, the Min ruler pleaded illness and refused an audience, sending his younger brother Jigong to receive him instead.

sentences.zh: 遺其禮部員外郎鄭元弼奉繼恭表隨損入貢。

translations.literal: He sent his Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites Zheng Yuanbi to present Jigong's memorial and accompany Sun in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Zheng Yuanbi of the Ministry of Rites to present Jigong's memorial and accompany Sun to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 閩主不禮於損，有士人林省鄒私謂損曰：「吾主不事其君，不愛其親，不恤其民，不敬其神，不睦其鄰，不禮其賓，其能久乎！

translations.literal: The Min ruler was discourteous to Sun; the scholar Lin Shengzou privately told Sun, "Our lord does not serve his sovereign, does not love his kin, does not care for his people, does not revere the spirits, does not befriend his neighbors, and does not honor his guests—how long can he last!
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler treated Sun rudely; a scholar named Lin Shengzou privately told him, "Our lord neglects his sovereign, his kin, and his people; he dishonors the spirits, alienates his neighbors, and insults his guests—how can such a rule endure?

sentences.zh: 余將僧服而北逃，會相見於上國耳。」

translations.literal: I shall don monk's robes and flee north; we shall meet again in the superior realm."
translations.idiomatic: I mean to take the tonsure and flee north—we shall meet again in your capital."

sentences.zh: 三月，庚戌，唐主追尊吳王恪為定宗孝靜皇帝，自曾祖以下皆追尊廟號及謚。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day gengxu, the Tang ruler posthumously honored Prince Wu Ke as Emperor Dingzong Xiaojing; from his great-grandfather downward all received posthumous temple names and epithets.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengxu day, the Tang ruler posthumously ennobled Prince Wu Li Ke as Emperor Dingzong Xiaojing and granted temple names and posthumous titles to his forebears back to his great-grandfather.

sentences.zh: 己未，詔歸德節度使劉知遠、忠武節度使杜重威並加同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, an edict added Liu Zhiyuan, Military Commissioner of Guide, and Du Chongwei, Military Commissioner of Zhongwu, both as Fellows of the Secretariat with the Tongpingzhangshi title.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day an edict made Liu Zhiyuan of Guide and Du Chongwei of Zhongwu both chief ministers with the Tongpingzhangshi title.

sentences.zh: 知遠自以有佐命功，重威起於外戚，無大功，恥與之同制。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan considered himself to have the merit of aiding the founding mandate; Chongwei had risen as a maternal relative without great achievement—he was ashamed to share the same appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan believed he had earned the throne by founding service, while Chongwei had risen only as an imperial in-law without comparable merit; he was ashamed to share the same rank.

sentences.zh: 制下數日，杜門四表辭不受。

translations.literal: Several days after the appointment was issued, he shut his doors and submitted four memorials declining to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of the decree he shut his gates and sent four memorials refusing the post.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謂趙瑩曰：「重威，朕之妹夫，知遠雖有功，何得堅拒制命！

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and said to Zhao Ying, "Chongwei is my brother-in-law; though Zhiyuan has merit, how dare he stubbornly refuse an imperial appointment!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and told Zhao Ying, "Chongwei is my brother-in-law; even if Zhiyuan has merit, how dare he defy an imperial appointment!

sentences.zh: 可落軍權，令歸私第！」

translations.literal: Strip him of military authority and send him home to his private residence!"
translations.idiomatic: Strip him of command and send him home!"

sentences.zh: 瑩拜請曰：「陛下昔在晉陽，兵不過五千，為唐兵十餘萬所攻，危於朝露，非知遠心如鐵石，豈能成大業！

translations.literal: Ying bowed and pleaded, "When Your Majesty was at Jinyang, your troops numbered no more than five thousand and were besieged by more than a hundred thousand Tang soldiers, in peril like the morning dew; had Zhiyuan's heart not been iron and stone, how could the great enterprise have been achieved!
translations.idiomatic: Ying bowed and pleaded, "At Jinyang Your Majesty had barely five thousand men against more than a hundred thousand Tang troops—peril thin as morning dew. Without Zhiyuan's iron resolve, the founding could never have succeeded!

sentences.zh: 奈何以小過棄之，竊恐此語外聞，非所以彰人君之大度也。」

translations.literal: How can you cast him aside for a small fault? I fear that if this remark is heard abroad, it will not display a ruler's great magnanimity."
translations.idiomatic: To discard him over a trifle—if word of this spreads abroad, it will not show the magnanimity a ruler should display."

sentences.zh: 帝意乃解，命端明殿學士和凝詣知遠第諭旨，知遠惶恐，起受命。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger then subsided; he ordered Academician He Ning of the Duanming Hall to go to Zhiyuan's residence to convey the imperial will, and Zhiyuan, in fear, rose and accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented and sent He Ning of the Duanming Hall to Zhiyuan's house with the imperial message; Zhiyuan, alarmed, rose and accepted.

sentences.zh: 尋州戌將王彥忠據懷遠城叛，上遣供奉官齊延祚往招諭之；

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhong, garrison commander of Xun Prefecture, seized Huaiyuan city and rebelled; the emperor sent Palace Attendant Qi Yanzuo to summon and persuade him;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhong, garrison commander of Xun, seized Huaiyuan and rebelled; the emperor sent palace attendant Qi Yanzuo to offer terms;

sentences.zh: 彥忠降，延祚殺之。

translations.literal: Yanzhong surrendered, and Yanzuo killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhong submitted, but Yanzuo killed him anyway.

sentences.zh: 上怒曰：「朕踐祚以來，未嘗失信於人，彥忠已輸仗出迎，延祚何得擅殺之！」

translations.literal: The emperor said in anger, "Since I ascended the throne I have never broken faith with anyone; Yanzhong had laid down his arms and come out to welcome him—how could Yanzuo kill him on his own authority!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged, "Since my accession I have never broken faith; Yanzhong had surrendered his arms and come out to submit—how dare Yanzuo kill him on his own!"

sentences.zh: 除延祚名，重杖配流，議者猶以為延祚不應免死。

translations.literal: Yanzuo was struck from the register, heavily caned, and exiled; commentators still held that he should not have escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzuo was struck from the rolls, heavily flogged, and exiled; many still thought he deserved execution.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，冊回鶻可汗仁美為奉化可汗。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, the Uyghur qaghan Renmei was enfeoffed as Qaghan of Fulfilled Submission.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day the Uyghur qaghan Renmei was invested as Qaghan of Fulfilled Submission.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，唐江王徐知證等請亦姓李；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Prince Jiang Xu Zhizheng of Tang and others asked also to take the surname Li;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Prince Jiang Xu Zhizheng and others asked permission to adopt the Li surname as well;

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，唐主祀南郊；

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, the Tang ruler sacrificed at the Southern Suburb;
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day the Tang ruler offered sacrifice at the Southern Suburb;

sentences.zh: 癸未，大赦。

translations.literal: on the day guiwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: on guiwei day he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖以來，軍國大政，天子多與崇政、樞密使議，宰相受成命，行制敕，講典故，治文事而已。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Taizu of Liang, on great matters of state and army the Son of Heaven often deliberated with the Commissioners of the Chongzheng and Bureau of Military Affairs; the chief ministers received settled decisions, issued edicts and orders, expounded precedents, and handled civil affairs only.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liang Taizu, emperors had usually decided military and state policy with the Chongzheng commissioners and the Bureau of Military Affairs; chief ministers merely executed orders, issued decrees, cited precedent, and handled paperwork.

sentences.zh: 帝懲唐明宗之世安重誨專橫，故即位之初，但命桑維翰兼樞密使。

translations.literal: The emperor, taking warning from An Chonghui's domineering conduct in the time of Tang Mingzong, at the start of his reign appointed only Sang Weihan additionally as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of An Chonghui's arrogance under Tang Mingzong, the emperor at his accession had appointed only Sang Weihan to double as commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 及劉處讓為樞密使，奏對多不稱旨，會處讓遭母喪，甲申，廢樞密院，以印付中書，院事皆委宰相分判。

translations.literal: When Liu Churang became Commissioner, his memorials and responses often failed to please; as Churang was in mourning for his mother, on the day jiashen the Bureau of Military Affairs was abolished, its seal given to the Secretariat, and its business entrusted to the chief ministers for divided adjudication.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Churang took the post, his audiences often missed the mark; when he entered mourning for his mother, on jiashen day the Bureau of Military Affairs was abolished, its seal handed to the Secretariat, and its duties divided among the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 以副使張從恩為宣徽使，直學士、倉部郎中司徒詡、工部郎中顏衎並罷守本官。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Zhang Cong'en was made Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat; Direct Academician and Director of the Bureau of Granaries Situ Xu and Director of the Bureau of Works Yan Kan were both dismissed to hold their original offices only.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commissioner Zhang Cong'en became palace commissioner; direct academician Situ Xu of the Granaries Bureau and Yan Kan of the Works Bureau were relieved to their original posts.

sentences.zh: 然勳臣近習不知大體，習於故事，每欲復之。

translations.literal: Yet meritorious ministers and intimate attendants, ignorant of larger principles and accustomed to precedent, often wished to restore it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet meritorious officials and court intimates, wedded to old practice and blind to larger policy, kept pressing for its restoration.

sentences.zh: 帝以唐之大臣除名在兩京者皆貧悴，復以李專美為贊善大夫，丙戌，以韓昭胤為兵部尚書，馬胤孫為太子賓客，房暠為右驍衛大將軍，並致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor, seeing that Tang ministers who had been dismissed and remained in the two capitals were all poor and wretched, restored Li Zhuanmei as Mentor of the Heir Apparent; on the day bingxu he appointed Han Zhaoyin Minister of War, Ma Yinsun Mentor to the Crown Prince, and Fang Gao General of the Right Valiant Guards—all as retired honors.
translations.idiomatic: Noting that dismissed Tang ministers languishing in the two capitals were destitute, the emperor restored Li Zhuanmei as mentor to the heir; on bingxu day he named Han Zhaoyin minister of war, Ma Yinsun mentor to the crown prince, and Fang Gao general of the right valiant guards—all honorific retirements.

sentences.zh: 閩主忌其叔父前建州刺史延武、戶部尚書延望才名，巫者林興與延武有怨，托鬼神語云：「延武、延望將為變。」

translations.literal: The Min ruler envied his uncles, the former Prefect of Jianzhou Yanwu and Minister of Revenue Yanwang, for their talent and fame; the shaman Lin Xing, who bore a grudge against Yanwu, spoke through spirits, saying, "Yanwu and Yanwang are about to rebel."
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler resented his uncles Yanwu, former prefect of Jian, and Yanwang, minister of revenue, for their renown; the shaman Lin Xing, who hated Yanwu, claimed the spirits said, "Yanwu and Yanwang are plotting rebellion."

sentences.zh: 閩主不復詰，使興帥壯士就第殺之，並其五子。

translations.literal: The Min ruler did not investigate further but sent Xing leading braves to their residences to kill them, together with their five sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler asked no more questions but sent Xing with strongmen to their homes to kill them and their five sons.

sentences.zh: 閩主用陳守元言，作三清殿於禁中，以黃金數千斤鑄寶皇大帝、天尊、老君像，晝夜作樂，焚香禱祀，求神丹。

translations.literal: Following Chen Shouyuan's advice, the Min ruler built the Hall of the Three Pure Ones within the palace, casting images of the August Emperor of Treasure, the Heavenly Venerable, and Lord Lao from several thousand jin of gold; day and night there was music, incense burning, and prayer for the elixir of immortality.
translations.idiomatic: At Chen Shouyuan's urging the Min ruler built the Hall of the Three Pure Ones in the palace and cast statues of the August Emperor, the Heavenly Venerable, and Lord Lao from thousands of jin of gold; day and night musicians played while he burned incense and prayed for the elixir of life.

sentences.zh: 政無大小，皆林興傳寶皇命決之。

translations.literal: Matters of government great and small were all decided by Lin Xing transmitting the commands of the August Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Great and small affairs of state were all decided by Lin Xing relaying the August Emperor's commands.

sentences.zh: 戊申，加楚王希範天策上將軍，賜印，聽開府置官屬。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, Prince Chu Xi Fan was advanced to Grand General of the Heavenly Stratagem, granted a seal, and permitted to open a staff office and appoint officials.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Prince Chu Ma Xifan was made Grand General of the Heavenly Stratagem, given a seal, and allowed to establish a staff with full appointments.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，唐徙吉王景遂為壽王，立壽陽公景達為宣城王。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, Tang transferred Prince Ji Jing Sui to be Prince Shou and installed the Duke of Shouyang Jing Da as Prince of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day Tang moved Prince Ji Li Jingsui to the title Prince of Shou and made Duke Jingda of Shouyang prince of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，唐鎮海節度使兼中書令梁懷王徐知諤卒。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, Xu Zhi'e, Prince of Lianghuai, Military Commissioner of Zhenhai and Concurrent Grand Councilor, died.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day Xu Zhi'e, Prince of Lianghuai, military commissioner of Zhenhai and concurrent grand councilor, died.

sentences.zh: 唐人遷讓皇之族於泰州，號永寧宮，防衛甚嚴。

translations.literal: The Tang people moved the clan of the Abdicated Emperor to Taizhou, calling it the Palace of Eternal Peace, with very strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang moved the abdicated emperor's kin to Taizhou in a compound called the Palace of Eternal Peace, under heavy guard.

sentences.zh: 康化節度使兼中書令楊珙稱疾，罷歸永寧宮。

translations.literal: Yang Gong, Military Commissioner of Kanghua and Concurrent Grand Councilor, claimed illness and retired to the Palace of Eternal Peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gong, military commissioner of Kanghua and concurrent grand councilor, pleaded illness and retired to the Palace of Eternal Peace.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以平盧節度使兼中書令楊璉為康化節度使；

translations.literal: On the day yichou, Yang Lian, Military Commissioner of Pinglu and Concurrent Grand Councilor, was appointed Military Commissioner of Kanghua;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day Yang Lian, military commissioner of Pinglu and concurrent grand councilor, was made military commissioner of Kanghua;

sentences.zh: 璉固辭，請終喪，從之。

translations.literal: Lian firmly declined and asked to complete his mourning; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Lian firmly declined and asked to finish mourning his father; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 唐主將立齊王璟為太子，固辭；

translations.literal: The Tang ruler was about to install Prince Qi Jing as crown prince; he firmly declined;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler wished to name Prince Qi Li Jing crown prince, but Jing firmly declined;

sentences.zh: 乃以為諸道兵馬大元帥、判六軍諸衛、守太尉、錄尚書事、升、揚二州牧。

translations.literal: he was instead made Grand Marshal of the Armies of All Circuits, Controller of the Six Armies and All Guards, Acting Grand Preceptor, Recorder of Affairs of the Department of State Affairs, and Governor of Sheng and Yang Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: instead he was made grand marshal of all circuits, controller of the six armies and guards, acting grand preceptor, recorder of the secretariat, and governor of Sheng and Yang.

sentences.zh: 閩判六軍諸衛建王繼嚴得士心，閩主忌之，六月，罷其兵柄，更名繼裕；

translations.literal: Prince Jian Jiyan, who controlled the Six Armies and All Guards in Min, had won the soldiers' hearts; the Min ruler envied him; in the sixth month his military authority was removed and his name changed to Jiyu;
translations.idiomatic: In Min, Prince Jian Jiyan, who commanded the six armies and guards, had won the troops' loyalty; the Min ruler resented this; in the sixth month he was stripped of command and renamed Jiyu;

sentences.zh: 以弟繼鏞判六軍，去諸衛字。

translations.literal: his younger brother Jiyong was put in charge of the Six Armies, dropping the words "and All Guards."
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Jiyong was put over the six armies, the "and guards" dropped from the title.

sentences.zh: 林興詐覺，流泉州。

translations.literal: Lin Xing's fraud was detected, and he was exiled to Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xing's deception was exposed and he was banished to Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 望氣者言宮中有災，乙未，閩主徙居長春宮。

translations.literal: A reader of omens said there was disaster in the palace; on the day yiwei the Min ruler moved to the Everlasting Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Geomancers warned of calamity within the palace; on yiwei day the Min ruler moved to the Everlasting Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day gengzi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, gengzi, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 成德節度使安重榮出於行伍，性粗率，恃勇驕暴，每謂人曰：「今世天子，兵強馬壯則為之耳。」

translations.literal: An Chongrong, Military Commissioner of Chengde, came from the ranks; his nature was coarse and blunt, and relying on courage he was arrogant and violent; he often told people, "In this age whoever has strong troops and sturdy horses can become Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: An Chongrong of Chengde was a common soldier risen to command—blunt, violent, and swollen with pride; he liked to say, "In our day whoever has the strongest army and horses can be emperor."

sentences.zh: 府廨有幡竿高數十尺，嘗挾弓矢謂左右曰：「我能中竿上龍首者，必有天命。」

translations.literal: At his headquarters there was a banner pole several tens of feet high; once, bow in hand, he told those beside him, "If I can hit the dragon head atop the pole, I must have Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: His headquarters had a banner pole dozens of feet tall; once, bow in hand, he told his attendants, "If I can hit the dragon's head on that pole, Heaven has chosen me."

sentences.zh: 一發中之，以是益自負。

translations.literal: With one shot he hit it, and thereby grew still more conceited.
translations.idiomatic: He struck it on the first shot and grew still more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 帝之遣重榮代秘瓊也，戒之曰：「瓊不受代，當別除汝一鎮，勿以力取，恐為患滋深。」

translations.literal: When the emperor sent Chongrong to replace Mi Qiong, he warned him, "If Qiong will not yield his post, I shall appoint you to another circuit—do not take it by force, lest trouble deepen."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sent Chongrong to replace Mi Qiong, he warned, "If Qiong refuses to step down, I will give you another circuit—do not seize it by force, or trouble will only grow."

sentences.zh: 重榮由是以帝為怯，謂人曰：「秘瓊匹夫耳，天子尚畏之，況我以將相之重，士馬之眾乎！」

translations.literal: Chongrong therefore took the emperor for timid and told people, "Mi Qiong is but a common fellow, yet the Son of Heaven still fears him—how much more so for one of my rank as general and minister, with masses of soldiers and horses!"
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong concluded the emperor was timid and said, "Mi Qiong is nobody, yet the emperor fears him—what of a man of my rank with armies at his back!"

sentences.zh: 每所奏請多逾分，為執政所可否，意憤憤不快，乃聚亡命，市戰馬，有飛揚之志。

translations.literal: His every memorial often exceeded proper bounds; when the administrators approved or denied them, he was resentful and displeased, and therefore gathered desperadoes, bought war horses, and harbored ambitions of soaring rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: His demands often overstepped bounds; when the court granted or denied them he seethed, gathered outlaws, bought war horses, and nursed rebellious ambitions.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，義武節度使皇甫遇與重榮姻家，甲辰，徙遇為昭義節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor knew of this; Huangfu Yu, Military Commissioner of Yiwu, was related to Chongrong by marriage; on the day jiachen Yu was transferred to be Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew; Huangfu Yu of Yiwu was related to Chongrong by marriage; on jiachen day Yu was transferred to Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，閩北宮火，焚宮殿殆盡。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, fire broke out in the Northern Palace of Min and burned the palaces nearly to completion.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day fire consumed the northern palace of Min and nearly destroyed it entirely.

sentences.zh: 戊申，薛融等上所定編敕，行之。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, Xue Rong and others presented to the emperor the compiled statutes they had drawn up, and they were put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Xue Rong and others presented the compiled statutes they had drafted, and they took effect.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，敕：「先令天下公私鑄錢，今私錢多用鉛錫，小弱缺薄，宜皆禁之，專令官司自鑄。」

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, an edict said, "Formerly both public and private coinage were permitted under Heaven; now private coin uses much lead and tin, is small, weak, thin, and defective—all should be forbidden, and only the authorities allowed to cast coin."
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day an edict declared, "Private minting was once allowed, but private coin is now debased with lead and tin—small, thin, and worthless. Ban it entirely and reserve minting to the state alone."

sentences.zh: 西京留守楊光遠疏中書侍郎、同平章事桑維翰遷除不公及營邸肆於兩都，與民爭利；

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan, Military Governor of the Western Capital, memorialized against Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow of the Secretariat Sang Weihan for unfair appointments and for operating inns and shops in the two capitals, competing with the people for profit;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan, governor of the western capital, accused chief minister Sang Weihan of unfair promotions and of running shops in both capitals at the people's expense;

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，閏月，壬申，出維翰為彰德節度使兼侍中。

translations.literal: the emperor had no choice; in the intercalary month, on the day renshen, he sent Weihan out as Military Commissioner of Zhangde and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor had no choice; in the intercalary month, on renshen day, he posted Weihan to Zhangde as military commissioner and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，義武節度使王處直子威，避王都之難，亡在契丹，至是，義武缺帥，契丹主遣使來言，「請使威襲父土地，如我朝之法。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Wei, son of Wang Chuzhi, Military Commissioner of Yiwu, had fled the troubles of Wang Du and was living among the Khitan; at this time Yiwu lacked a commander, and the Khitan ruler sent envoys saying, "Let Wei inherit his father's lands, as in our court's law."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Wei, son of Yiwu's Wang Chuzhi, had fled Wang Du's revolt and taken refuge with the Khitan; now Yiwu lacked a commander, and the Khitan ruler sent envoys asking that Wei inherit his father's domain "as our law provides."

sentences.zh: 帝辭以「中國之法必自刺史、團練、防禦序遷乃至節度使，請遣威至此，漸加進用。」

translations.literal: The emperor declined, saying, "By the law of China one must advance in order from prefect, training commissioner, and defense commissioner up to military commissioner; send Wei here and he shall be promoted step by step."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, citing Chinese practice: "One rises from prefect through training and defense commissioner to military commissioner—send Wei here and we will promote him in due course."

sentences.zh: 契丹主怒，復遣使來言曰：「爾自節度使為天子，亦有階級邪！」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler was angry and again sent envoys saying, "You yourself went from military commissioner to Son of Heaven—do you also have ranks and steps!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler was furious and sent envoys again: "You yourself rose from military commissioner to emperor—do ranks matter for you or not!"

sentences.zh: 帝恐其滋蔓不已，厚賂契丹，且請以處直兄孫彰德節度使廷胤為義武節度使以厭其意。

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing the matter would spread without end, richly bribed the Khitan and also asked that Tingyin, grandson of Chuzhi's elder brother and Military Commissioner of Zhangde, be made Military Commissioner of Yiwu to satisfy their wish.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the dispute would widen, the emperor lavished gifts on the Khitan and offered Wang Tingyin of Zhangde, Chuzhi's grandnephew, as military commissioner of Yiwu to appease them.

sentences.zh: 契丹怒稍解。

translations.literal: The Khitan anger was somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler's anger eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 初，閩惠宗以太祖元從為拱宸、按鶴都，及康宗立，更募壯士二千人為腹心，號宸衛都，祿賜皆厚於二都；

translations.literal: Earlier, Min Huizong had made the founding followers the Palatial Guard and Crane-Pressing Commands; when Kangzong succeeded, he recruited two thousand more stalwarts as his inner guard, called the Imperial Guard Command, with salaries and gifts all richer than the two older commands;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Min Huizong had organized the founding companions into the Palatial Guard and Crane-Pressing commands; when Kangzong took the throne he recruited two thousand more elite troops as his personal guard, the Imperial Guard command, with pay and gifts exceeding the older units;

sentences.zh: 或言二都怨望，將作亂，閩主欲分隸漳、泉二州，二都益怒。

translations.literal: some said the two commands were resentful and about to rebel; the Min ruler wished to divide them and attach them to Zhang and Quan Prefectures, and the two commands grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: rumors spread that the two older commands were mutinous; the Min ruler planned to split them between Zhang and Quan prefectures, which only inflamed them further.

sentences.zh: 閩主好為長夜之飲，強群臣酒，醉則令左右伺其過失；

translations.literal: The Min ruler loved all-night drinking, forced wine on his ministers, and when they were drunk ordered attendants to watch for their faults;
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler loved all-night banquets, forced his ministers to drink, and when they were drunk had attendants spy on their missteps;

sentences.zh: 從弟繼隆醉失禮，斬之。

translations.literal: his cousin Jilong, drunk, committed a breach of etiquette, and was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: his cousin Jilong, drunk and discourteous, was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 屢以猜怒誅宗室，叔父左僕射、同平章事延羲陽為狂愚以避禍，閩主賜以道士服，置武夷山中；

translations.literal: Repeatedly, out of suspicious anger, he executed members of the imperial clan; his uncle Yanxi, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow of the Secretariat, pretended to madness and folly to escape disaster; the Min ruler bestowed Taoist robes upon him and placed him in Mount Wuyi;
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he killed kinsmen on mere suspicion; his uncle Yanxi, chief minister of Min, feigned idiocy to survive, was given Taoist garb, and was sent to live on Mount Wuyi;

sentences.zh: 尋復召還，幽於私第。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned back and confined in a private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yanxi was recalled and kept under house arrest.

sentences.zh: 閩主數侮拱宸、控鶴軍使永泰朱文進、光山連重遇，二人怨之。

translations.literal: The Min ruler repeatedly insulted Zhu Wenjin of Yongtai and Lian Chongyu of Guangshan, commanders of the Palatial Guard and Crane-Pressing armies; the two harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler often humiliated Zhu Wenjin and Lian Chongyu, who commanded the Palatial Guard and Crane-Pressing corps, and both men came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 會北宮火，求賊不獲；

translations.literal: When the northern palace caught fire and the culprit could not be found;
translations.idiomatic: Then the northern palace burned, and no arsonist could be found;

sentences.zh: 閩主命重遇將內外營兵掃除餘燼，日役萬人，士卒甚苦之。

translations.literal: the Min ruler ordered Chongyu to lead inner and outer camp troops to sweep away the remaining embers, conscripting ten thousand men a day—the soldiers suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: the Min ruler put Chongyu in charge of ten thousand men a day from the inner and outer camps to clear the ashes, and the troops were driven to misery.

sentences.zh: 又疑重遇知縱火之謀，欲誅之；

translations.literal: He further suspected that Chongyu knew of the arson plot and wished to execute him;
translations.idiomatic: He also suspected Chongyu of complicity in the fire and planned to kill him;

sentences.zh: 內學士陳郯私告重遇。

translations.literal: Inner Academician Chen Tan privately informed Chongyu.
translations.idiomatic: the inner academician Chen Tan warned Chongyu in secret.

sentences.zh: 辛巳夜，重遇入直，帥二都兵焚長春宮以攻閩主，使人迎延羲於瓦礫中，呼萬歲；

translations.literal: On the night of xinsi, Chongyu entered duty, led the troops of both commands to burn the Changchun Palace and attack the Min ruler, sent men to welcome Yanxi from amid the rubble, and cried "Long live [the emperor]!"
translations.idiomatic: That night, xinsi day, Chongyu went on palace duty, rallied both guard corps, set Changchun Palace ablaze, and marched on the Min ruler; his men hauled Yanxi from the ruins and shouted acclamation.

sentences.zh: 復召外營兵共攻閩主；

translations.literal: He again summoned outer-camp troops to join in attacking the Min ruler;
translations.idiomatic: He then called in the outer garrison to strike the Min ruler together;

sentences.zh: 獨宸衛都拒戰，閩主乃與李-{后}-如宸衛都。

translations.literal: only the Imperial Guard command refused battle; the Min ruler then went with Empress Li to the Imperial Guard command.
translations.idiomatic: only the Imperial Guard held its ground; the Min ruler fled with Empress Li to join them.

sentences.zh: 比明，亂兵焚宸衛都，宸衛都戰敗，餘眾千餘人奉閩主及李-{后}-出北關，至梧桐嶺，眾稍逃散。

translations.literal: By dawn the mutineers had burned the Imperial Guard command; the guard was defeated, and a little over a thousand survivors escorted the Min ruler and Empress Li out the north gate to Wutong Ridge, where the crowd gradually scattered.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the rebels torched the Imperial Guard camp and broke them; a thousand-odd survivors shepherded the Min ruler and Empress Li through the north gate to Wutong Ridge, but the party steadily melted away.

sentences.zh: 延羲使兄子前汀州剌史繼業將兵追之，及於村舍；

translations.literal: Yanxi sent his elder brother's son, former prefect of Tingzhou Jiye, with troops in pursuit and caught up at a village;
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi dispatched his nephew Jiye, lately prefect of Ting, with troops in pursuit and overtook them at a hamlet;

sentences.zh: 閩主素善射，引弓殺數人。

translations.literal: The Min ruler had long been skilled at archery; he drew his bow and killed several men.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler was a fine archer and shot down several pursuers.

sentences.zh: 俄而追兵雲集，閩主知不免，投弓謂繼業曰：「卿臣節安在！」

translations.literal: Soon the pursuers gathered thick; knowing he could not escape, the Min ruler cast aside his bow and said to Jiye, "Where is your minister's fidelity!"
translations.idiomatic: Before long the chase closed in; seeing the end, the Min ruler dropped his bow and cried to Jiye, "Where is your loyalty as a subject!"

sentences.zh: 繼業曰：「君無君德，臣安有臣節！

translations.literal: Jiye replied, "When the ruler lacks the virtues of a ruler, how can the minister have the fidelity of a minister!
translations.idiomatic: Jiye answered, "A lord without lordly virtue earns no subject's loyalty!

sentences.zh: 新君，叔父也，舊君，昆弟也，孰親孰疏？」

translations.literal: The new ruler is my uncle; the old ruler is my cousin—which is closer, which more distant?"
translations.idiomatic: The new sovereign is my uncle; the old one is my cousin—which bond should weigh more?"

sentences.zh: 閩主不復言。

translations.literal: The Min ruler said nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler fell silent.

sentences.zh: 繼業與之俱還，至陀莊，飲以酒，醉而縊之，並李-{后}-及諸子、王繼恭皆死。

translations.literal: Jiye returned with him to Tuozhuang, gave him wine, and when he was drunk strangled him; Empress Li, all the sons, and Wang Jigong died as well.
translations.idiomatic: Jiye brought him back to Tuozhuang, plied him with wine, and strangled him once he was drunk; Empress Li, the princes, and Wang Jigong all perished with him.

sentences.zh: 宸衛餘眾奔吳越。

translations.literal: The remaining Imperial Guard troops fled to Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors of the Imperial Guard escaped into Wuyue territory.

sentences.zh: 延羲自稱威武節度使、閩國王，更名曦，改元永隆，赦系囚，頒賚中外。

translations.literal: Yanxi styled himself Military Commissioner of Weiwu and King of Min, changed his name to Xi, adopted the era name Yonglong, pardoned prisoners, and distributed rewards throughout the court and realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi proclaimed himself military commissioner of Weiwu and king of Min, took the name Xi, declared the Yonglong era, freed prisoners, and showered gifts on court and country alike.

sentences.zh: 以宸衛弒閩主赴於鄰國；

translations.literal: He sent the Imperial Guard, which had murdered the Min ruler, into exile in a neighboring state;
translations.idiomatic: He banished the Imperial Guard that had killed the Min ruler to a neighboring realm;

sentences.zh: 謚閩主曰聖神英睿文明廣武應道大弘孝皇帝，廟號康宗。

translations.literal: he gave the posthumous title Emperor Sageship, Spiritual Wisdom, Civil Brilliance, Broad Martiality, Responsive to the Way, Greatly Magnanimous in Filial Piety, with temple name Kangzong.
translations.idiomatic: and posthumously ennobled the fallen ruler with the grand temple name Kangzong and an equally grand honorific title.

sentences.zh: 遣商人間道奉表稱籓於晉；

translations.literal: He sent merchants by secret routes to present a memorial declaring himself vassal to Jin;
translations.idiomatic: Through covert traders he sent tribute and a memorial submitting to Jin as a vassal;

sentences.zh: 然其在國，置百官皆如天子之制。

translations.literal: yet within his realm he appointed the hundred officials all in the manner of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: yet at home he staffed every office as if he were emperor in his own right.

sentences.zh: 以太子太傅致仕李真為司空兼中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: He appointed Li Zhen, retired Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, as Grand Minister of Works, Concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Fellow of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He named the retired grand mentor Li Zhen grand minister of works and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 連重遇之攻康宗也，陳守元在宮中，易服將逃，兵人殺之。

translations.literal: When Lian Chongyu attacked Kangzong, Chen Shouyuan was in the palace, changed clothes to flee, and the soldiers killed him.
translations.idiomatic: During Chongyu's assault on Kangzong, Chen Shouyuan was inside the palace changing clothes to flee when the mutineers cut him down.

sentences.zh: 重遇執蔡守蒙，數以賣官之罪而斬之。

translations.literal: Chongyu seized Cai Shoumeng, enumerated his crime of selling offices, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyu seized Cai Shoumeng, denounced him for selling offices, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 閩王曦既立，遣使誅林興於泉州。

translations.literal: After King Xi of Min had been enthroned, he sent envoys to execute Lin Xing at Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once King Xi of Min was secure on the throne, he sent agents to kill Lin Xing at Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 河決亳州。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst its banks at Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River broke through its dikes at Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛丑，以馮道守司徒兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinchou day, Feng Dao was ordered to hold the post of Grand Mentor and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinchou day, Feng Dao was confirmed as grand mentor and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，詔中書知印止委上相，由是事無鉅細，悉委於道。

translations.literal: On renyin day an edict decreed that custody of the Secretariat seal should rest solely with the chief minister; henceforth matters great and small were all entrusted to Dao.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day the throne ruled that only the senior chief minister might hold the Secretariat seal, and from then on every affair, large or small, passed through Dao alone.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗訪以軍謀，對曰：「征伐大事，在聖心獨斷。

translations.literal: The emperor once consulted him on military plans; he replied, "Matters of campaign and conquest rest on the sage heart's sole decision.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked his view on strategy, Dao answered, "War and conquest are for the sacred mind alone to decide.

sentences.zh: 臣書生，惟知謹守歷代成規而已。」

translations.literal: Your servant is a bookish man and knows only to hold fast to the established rules of successive dynasties."
translations.idiomatic: I am only a scholar and can advise you to keep to the precedents of former dynasties."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the answer.

sentences.zh: 道嘗稱疾求退，帝使鄭王重貴詣第省之，曰：「來日不出，朕當親往。」

translations.literal: Dao once pleaded illness and asked to retire; the emperor sent Prince of Zheng Chonggui to his residence to inquire of him, saying, "If you do not appear tomorrow, I shall come in person."
translations.idiomatic: Dao once feigned illness and sought retirement; the emperor sent Prince of Zheng Chonggui to visit him with the warning, "If you do not attend court tomorrow, I will come to your house myself."

sentences.zh: 道乃出視事。

translations.literal: Dao then came out to attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dao thereupon returned to office.

sentences.zh: 當時寵遇，群臣無與為比。

translations.literal: At that time his favor and treatment had no equal among the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: No other minister enjoyed such trust and privilege.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以吳越王元瓘為天下兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: On jiyou day the King of Wuyue, Qian Yuanguan, was made Commander-in-Chief of All Armies under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day Qian Yuanguan of Wuyue was named commander-in-chief of all armies under heaven.

sentences.zh: 黔南巡內溪州刺史彭士愁引蔣、錦州蠻萬餘人寇辰、澧州，焚掠鎮戍，遣使乞師於蜀；

translations.literal: Peng Shichou, inner prefect of Xunnei in Qiannan, led more than ten thousand Man of Jiang and Jin prefectures to raid Chen and Li prefectures, burning and plundering fortified posts, and sent envoys to Shu to beg troops;
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shichou, inner prefect of Xunnei in southern Qian, rallied more than ten thousand tribal warriors from Jiang and Jin to storm Chen and Li, burn frontier posts, and ask Shu for reinforcements;

sentences.zh: 蜀主以道遠，不許。

translations.literal: the Shu ruler, citing the distance, refused.
translations.idiomatic: but the Shu ruler, pleading distance, declined.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛未，楚王希範命左靜江指揮使劉勍、決勝指揮使廖匡齊帥衡山兵五千討之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinwei day, King Xifan of Chu ordered Left Commander of the Tranquil River Liu Peng and Victory Commander Liao Kuangqi to lead five thousand troops from Hengshan to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinwei day, King Xifan of Chu sent Liu Peng of the Tranquil River command and Liao Kuangqi of the Victory command with five thousand Hengshan troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以唐許王從益為郇國公，奉唐祀。

translations.literal: On guiwei day Tang's Prince of Xu, Congyi, was made Duke of Xun to maintain the sacrifices of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day the Tang heir Congyi, Prince of Xu, was enfeoffed as Duke of Xun to keep the Tang ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 從益尚幼，李-{后}-養從益於宮中，奉王淑妃如事母。

translations.literal: Congyi was still young; Empress Li raised him in the palace and had Princess Consort Wang Shufei served as to a mother.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi was still a child; Empress Li reared him in the palace and had him honor Princess Consort Wang Shufei as a mother.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚戌，閩康宗所遣使者鄭元弼至大梁。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on gengxu day, the envoy Zheng Yuanbi sent by Min's Kangzong reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on gengxu day, Kangzong's envoy Zheng Yuanbi arrived at the Later Jin capital, Daliang.

sentences.zh: 康宗遺執政書曰：「閩國一從興運，久歷年華，見北辰之帝座頻移，致東海之風帆多阻。」

translations.literal: Kangzong left a letter to the chief ministers saying, "Min has followed the turning of fortune since the beginning and has endured many years; we have seen the throne of the northern asterism shift again and again, so that sails on the eastern sea meet many obstacles."
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong's letter to the Jin ministers read, "Min has ridden the tide of empire for many years, yet as the northern throne keeps changing hands, our ships on the eastern sea are repeatedly blocked from paying court."

sentences.zh: 又求用敵國禮致書往來。

translations.literal: He also asked that correspondence be conducted with the ceremonial forms used between equal states.
translations.idiomatic: He also demanded that future letters follow the etiquette reserved for equal powers.

sentences.zh: 帝怒其不遜，壬子，詔卻其貢物及福、建諸州綱運，並令元弼及進奏官林恩部送速歸。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered by this insolence; on renzi day he ordered their tribute goods and the tax shipments from Fu, Jian, and other prefectures refused, and commanded Yuanbi and memorial presenter Lin En escorted swiftly home.
translations.idiomatic: Outraged by the presumption, the emperor on renzi day rejected their gifts and the tax convoys from Fu, Jian, and neighboring prefectures, and ordered Yuanbi and the memorial officer Lin En sent home at once under escort.

sentences.zh: 兵部員外郎李知損上言：「王昶僭慢，宜執留使者，籍沒其貨。」

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Ministry of War Li Zhisun memorialized, "Wang Chang's arrogance deserves that we detain the envoys and confiscate their goods."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhisun of the War Ministry urged, "Wang Chang is insolent; hold the envoys and seize their cargo."

sentences.zh: 乃下元弼、恩獄。

translations.literal: Yuanbi and En were therefore thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbi and Lin En were jailed.

sentences.zh: 吳越恭穆夫人馬氏卒。

translations.literal: The Respectful and Solemn Lady Ma of Wuyue died.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ma, styled Respectful and Solemn, consort of Wuyue, died.

sentences.zh: 夫人，雄武節度使綽之女也。

translations.literal: The lady was the daughter of Qian Chuo, Military Commissioner of Xiongwu.
translations.idiomatic: She was the daughter of Qian Chuo, military commissioner of Xiongwu.

sentences.zh: 初，武肅王鏐禁中外畜聲妓，文穆王元瓘年三十餘無子，夫人為之請於鏐，鏐喜曰：「吾家祭祀，汝實主之。」

translations.literal: Earlier King Wusu Qian Liu had forbidden court and country to keep singing girls and entertainers; King Wenmu Yuanguan was past thirty without a son, and the lady petitioned Liu on his behalf; Liu was pleased and said, "The sacrifices of our house—you in truth preside over them."
translations.idiomatic: Long before, King Wusu Qian Liu had banned music girls throughout his realm; Yuanguan passed thirty childless, and his wife pleaded with Liu, who rejoiced and said, "Our line's sacrifices rest on you alone."

sentences.zh: 乃聽元瓘納妾。

translations.literal: He then allowed Yuanguan to take concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Liu then let Yuanguan take concubines.

sentences.zh: 鹿氏，生弘僔、弘倧；

translations.literal: Lady Lu bore Hongpu and Hongzong;
translations.idiomatic: Lu bore Hongpu and Hongzong;

sentences.zh: 許氏，生弘佐；

translations.literal: Lady Xu bore Hongzuo;
translations.idiomatic: Xu bore Hongzuo;

sentences.zh: 吳氏，生弘俶；

translations.literal: Lady Wu bore Hongchu;
translations.idiomatic: Wu bore Hongchu;

sentences.zh: 眾妾生弘偡，弘億、弘儀、弘偓、弘仰、弘信；

translations.literal: the other concubines bore Hongsi, Hongyi, Hongyi, Hongwo, Hongyang, and Hongxin;
translations.idiomatic: the lesser consorts bore Hongsi, Hongyi, Hongyi, Hongwo, Hongyang, and Hongxin;

sentences.zh: 夫人撫視慈愛如一。

translations.literal: the lady nursed and loved them all alike.
translations.idiomatic: yet the principal wife raised every child with equal tenderness.

sentences.zh: 常置銀鹿於帳前，坐諸兒於上而弄之。

translations.literal: She often placed a silver deer before the curtained bed, seated the children upon it, and played with them.
translations.idiomatic: She kept a silver deer by her couch, set the boys on its back, and played with them there.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊子，契丹遣其臣遙折來使，遂如吳越。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuzi day, the Khitan sent their minister Yaozhe as envoy, who then proceeded to Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuzi day, the Khitan dispatched Yaozhe as envoy, and he continued on to Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 楚王希範始開天策府，置護軍都尉、領軍司馬等官，以諸弟及將校為之。

translations.literal: King Xifan of Chu first opened the Celestial Policy Bureau, appointing Guard Commandant, Army Marshal, and other posts, giving them to his brothers and generals.
translations.idiomatic: King Xifan of Chu founded the Celestial Policy Bureau, creating posts such as guard commandant and army marshal for his brothers and commanders.

sentences.zh: 又以幕僚拓跋恆、李弘皋、廖匡圖、徐仲雅等十八人為學士。

translations.literal: He also made eighteen staff members—Tuoba Heng, Li Honggao, Liao Kuangtu, Xu Zhongya, and others—academicians.
translations.idiomatic: He named eighteen advisers, including Tuoba Heng, Li Honggao, Liao Kuangtu, and Xu Zhongya, as bureau scholars.

sentences.zh: 劉勍等進攻溪州，彭士愁兵敗，棄州走保山寨；

translations.literal: Liu Peng and the others advanced on Xizhou; Peng Shichou's army was defeated, and he abandoned the prefecture and fled to a mountain stronghold;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Peng pressed into Xizhou; Peng Shichou was routed, abandoned the city, and retreated to a cliffside fort;

sentences.zh: 石崖四絕，勍為梯棧上圍之。

translations.literal: the stone cliffs were sheer on four sides; Peng built ladders and galleries to ascend and besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: with cliffs on every side Peng erected scaling ladders and walkways to invest the height.

sentences.zh: 廖匡齊戰死，楚王希範遣吊其母，其母不哭，謂使者曰：「廖氏三百口受王溫飽之賜，舉族效死，未足以報，況一子乎！

translations.literal: Liao Kuangqi died in battle; King Xifan of Chu sent condolences to his mother; she did not weep and told the envoy, "The Liao household of three hundred mouths has long eaten the king's bounty; the whole clan would die in his service and still not repay it—what is one son!
translations.idiomatic: Liao Kuangqi fell in the fighting; King Xifan sent condolences to his mother, who refused to mourn and told the messenger, "Three hundred Liao mouths have fed at the king's table; our clan owes him our lives—why grieve for one son?

sentences.zh: 願王無以為念。」

translations.literal: I ask that the king give the matter no further thought."
translations.idiomatic: Tell the king not to trouble himself on our account."

sentences.zh: 王以其母為賢，厚恤其家。

translations.literal: The king, deeming her virtuous, richly compensated her family.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by her nobility, the king lavished rewards on her household.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙戌，禁刱造佛寺。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingxu day, the building of new Buddhist temples was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingxu day, the throne banned the construction of new Buddhist temples.

sentences.zh: 閩王作新宮，徙居之。

translations.literal: The King of Min built a new palace and moved into it.
translations.idiomatic: The Min king finished a new palace and took up residence there.

sentences.zh: 是歲，漢門下侍郎、同平章事趙光裔言於漢主曰：「自馬後崩，未嘗通使於楚，親鄰舊好，不可忘也。」

translations.literal: That year, Zhao Guangyi, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow of the Secretariat of Han, said to the Han ruler, "Since Empress Ma died, we have not exchanged envoys with Chu; the old ties of kinship and neighborhood must not be forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: That year Han chief minister Zhao Guangyi told his sovereign, "Since Empress Ma's death we have sent no envoys to Chu, yet that neighbor is kin by marriage and should not be neglected."

sentences.zh: 因薦諫議大夫李紓可以將命，漢主從之；

translations.literal: He therefore recommended Remonstrance Officer Li Shu as fit to bear the mission, and the Han ruler agreed;
translations.idiomatic: He recommended remonstrance officer Li Shu as envoy, and the Han ruler assented;

sentences.zh: 楚亦遣使報聘。

translations.literal: Chu also sent envoys in return.
translations.idiomatic: Chu reciprocated with envoys of its own.

sentences.zh: 光裔相漢二十餘年，府庫充實，邊境無虞。

translations.literal: Guangyi had served Han as chief minister for more than twenty years; the treasury was full and the borders untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyi had governed Han for over twenty years, filling the coffers and keeping the frontiers quiet.

sentences.zh: 及卒，漢主復以其子翰林學士承旨、尚書左丞損為門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: When he died, the Han ruler again appointed his son Sun, Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the Han ruler promoted his son Sun, a Hanlin expositor and vice director, to chief minister in his father's place.

sentences.zh: 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝中天福五年（

translations.literal: Gaozu the Sagely, Civil, Martial, Virtuous, Filial Emperor, middle year of Tianfu five (
translations.idiomatic: Reign of Emperor Gaozu of Later Jin, fifth year of Tianfu (

sentences.zh: 庚子，公元九四零年）

translations.literal: gengzi, AD 940)
translations.idiomatic: gengzi, the year 940 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，帝引見閩使鄭元弼等。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the emperor granted audience to the Min envoys Zheng Yuanbi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the emperor received the Min envoys led by Zheng Yuanbi.

sentences.zh: 元弼曰：「王昶蠻夷之君，不知禮義，陛下得其善言不足喜，惡言不足怒。

translations.literal: Yuanbi said, "King Chang is a barbarian lord who knows nothing of ritual; whether Your Majesty hears fair words or foul from him should neither delight nor anger you.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbi said, "King Chang is a frontier ruler ignorant of ceremony; good words or bad from him should neither please nor vex Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣將命無狀，願伏鈇鍎以贖昶罪。」

translations.literal: Your servant performed his commission badly and begs to accept the axe to redeem Chang's offense."
translations.idiomatic: I alone failed in my mission and beg to die in his stead."

sentences.zh: 帝憐之，辛未，詔釋元弼等。

translations.literal: The emperor took pity on him; on xinwei day he decreed the release of Yuanbi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved; on xinwei day he ordered Yuanbi and his party freed.

sentences.zh: 楚劉勍等因大風，以火箭焚彭士愁寨而攻之，士愁帥麾下逃入獎、錦深山，乙未，遣其子師暠帥諸酋長納溪、錦、獎三州印，請降於楚。

translations.literal: Liu Peng and the others of Chu, taking advantage of a strong wind, fired burning arrows into Peng Shichou's stockade and attacked; Shichou led his followers into the deep mountains of Jiang and Jin; on yiwei day he sent his son Shigao at the head of the chieftains to surrender the seals of Xi, Jin, and Jiang prefectures and submit to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Peng exploited a gale to rain fire-arrows on Peng Shichou's camp; Shichou fled into the Jiang-Jin highlands, and on yiwei day his son Shigao led the tribal chiefs in surrendering the seals of Xi, Jin, and Jiang to Chu.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚戌，北都留守、同平章事安彥威入朝，上曰：「吾所重者信與義。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengxu day, An Yanwei, Military Governor of the Northern Capital and Fellow of the Secretariat, came to court; the emperor said, "What I value are trust and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengxu day, northern capital governor An Yanwei arrived at court; the emperor told him, "I hold trust and duty above all.

sentences.zh: 昔契丹以義救我，我今以信報之；

translations.literal: In former days the Khitan aided us out of righteousness; today I repay them in good faith;
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan once saved us from righteousness; now I repay them in good faith;

sentences.zh: 聞其徵求不已，公能屈節奉之，深稱朕意。」

translations.literal: hearing that their demands never cease, if you can humble yourself in serving them, you will deeply accord with my intent."
translations.idiomatic: their exactions never end, and if you can bow to their demands you will serve my purpose well."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下以蒼生之故，猶卑辭厚幣以事之，臣何屈節之有！」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty, for the sake of the common people, still speaks softly and sends rich gifts to serve them—how could your servant call that humiliation!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei answered, "Your Majesty already humbles himself and heaps gifts on them for the people's sake—what humiliation is there for me!"

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 劉勍引兵還長沙。

translations.literal: Liu Peng led his troops back to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Peng marched his army back to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 楚王希範徙溪州於便地，表彭士愁為溪州刺史，以劉勍為錦州刺史；

translations.literal: King Xifan of Chu moved Xizhou to a more convenient site, memorialized Peng Shichou as prefect of Xi, and appointed Liu Peng prefect of Jin;
translations.idiomatic: King Xifan relocated Xizhou to easier ground, installed Peng Shichou as its prefect, and made Liu Peng prefect of Jin;

sentences.zh: 自是群蠻服於楚。

translations.literal: from this the various Man submitted to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: after which the hill tribes submitted to Chu.

sentences.zh: 希範自謂伏波之後，以銅五千斤鑄柱，高丈二尺，入地六尺，銘誓狀於上，立之溪州。

translations.literal: Xifan, claiming descent from the Pacifier of Waves, cast a bronze pillar five thousand catties in weight, twelve feet high with six feet set in the earth, inscribed the oath upon it, and erected it at Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Boasting descent from Ma Yuan the Wave-Pacifier, Xifan cast a five-thousand-catties bronze pillar twelve feet tall, six feet buried, engraved a sworn pact on it, and set it up at Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 唐康化節度使兼中書令楊璉謁平陵還，一夕，大醉，卒於舟中，唐主追封謚曰弘農靖王。

translations.literal: Yang Lian of Tang, Military Commissioner of Kanghua and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, returned from paying respects at the imperial tombs; one night, greatly drunk, he died aboard his boat; the Tang ruler posthumously enfeoffed and titled him King Jing of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang's Yang Lian, military commissioner of Kanghua and director of the secretariat, came back from tomb rites at the Tang mausolea, drank himself insensible one night aboard his boat, and died; the Tang court posthumously ennobled him King Jing of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 閩王曦既立，驕淫苛虐，猜忌宗族，多尋舊怨。

translations.literal: After King Xi of Min had been enthroned, he was arrogant, licentious, harsh, and cruel, suspicious of the clan, and often pursued old grudges.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, King Xi of Min grew arrogant, debauched, and cruel, eyed his kinsmen with suspicion, and hunted old scores.

sentences.zh: 其弟建州刺史延政數以書諫之，曦怒，復書罵之；

translations.literal: His younger brother Yanzheng, prefect of Jian, repeatedly remonstrated by letter; Xi was angry and answered with letters of abuse;
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yanzheng, prefect of Jian, wrote again and again to remonstrate; Xi answered with scathing letters;

sentences.zh: 遣親吏業翹監建州軍，教練使杜漢崇監南鎮軍，二人爭捃延政陰事告於曦，由是兄弟積相猜恨。

translations.literal: he sent trusted officials Ye Qiao to supervise the Jian army and Training Commissioner Du Hanchong to supervise the southern garrison; the two vied to gather Yanzheng's secrets and report them to Xi, so the brothers' mutual suspicion and hatred deepened.
translations.idiomatic: he posted his confidant Ye Qiao over the Jian army and training commissioner Du Hanchong over the southern camp; both men raced to dig up Yanzheng's secrets for Xi, and hatred between the brothers mounted.

sentences.zh: 一日，翹與延政議事不葉，翹訶之曰：「公反邪！」

translations.literal: One day Qiao and Yanzheng could not agree in council; Qiao reviled him, saying, "My lord, are you rebelling!"
translations.idiomatic: One day Qiao quarreled with Yanzheng in council and shouted, "Are you raising rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 延政怒，欲斬翹；

translations.literal: Yanzheng was angry and wished to behead Qiao;
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng flew into a rage and tried to execute him;

sentences.zh: 翹奔南鎮，延政發兵就攻之，敗其戍兵。

translations.literal: Qiao fled to the southern garrison; Yanzheng raised troops to attack it and defeated its garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao ran to the southern camp; Yanzheng marched on it and routed the garrison.

sentences.zh: 翹、漢崇奔福州，西鄙戍兵皆潰。

translations.literal: Qiao and Hanchong fled to Fuzhou, and the western border garrisons all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao and Hanchong fled to Fuzhou, and the western outposts melted away.

sentences.zh: 二月，曦遣統軍使潘師逵、吳行真將兵四萬擊延政。

translations.literal: In the second month Xi sent Army Controller Pan Shikui and Wu Xingzhen with forty thousand troops to strike Yanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Xi dispatched Pan Shikui and Wu Xingzhen with forty thousand men against Yanzheng.

sentences.zh: 師逵軍於建州城西，行真軍於城南，皆阻水置營，焚城外廬舍。

translations.literal: Shikui encamped west of Jian city and Xingzhen south of the city; both set camps across the water and burned the dwellings outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Shikui pitched west of Jian and Xingzhen south of it; each camped beyond the river and torched the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 延政求救於吳越，壬戌，吳越王元瓘遣寧國節度使、同平章事仰仁詮、內都監使薛萬忠將兵四萬救之，丞相林鼎諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Yanzheng sought rescue from Wuyue. On renxu, King Yuan Guan of Wuyue sent Ningguo military commissioner and Grand Councilor Yang Renquan and inner palace commissioner Xue Wanzhong to lead forty thousand troops to save him; Chancellor Lin Ding remonstrated, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng called on Wuyue for help. On renxu, King Yuan Guan of Wuyue dispatched Yang Renquan, military commissioner of Ningguo and Grand Councilor, and Xue Wanzhong, inner palace commissioner, with forty thousand men to relieve him. Chancellor Lin Ding urged against it; the king paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊辰，師逵分兵三千，遣都軍使蔡弘裔將之出戰，延政遣其將林漢徹等敗之於茶山，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuchen, Shikui divided off three thousand troops and sent Army Controller Cai Hongyi to lead them out to fight; Yanzheng sent his generals Lin Hanche and others to defeat them at Mount Cha, beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuchen, Shikui detached three thousand men under Army Controller Cai Hongyi for a sortie. Yanzheng sent Lin Hanche and other commanders to rout them at Mount Cha and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 安彥威、王建立皆請致仕；

translations.literal: An Yanwei and Wang Jianli both requested to retire from office;
translations.idiomatic: Both An Yanwei and Wang Jianli asked permission to retire;

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以歸德節度使、侍衛馬步都指揮使、同平章事劉知遠為鄴都留守，徙彥威為歸德節度使，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: On xinwei, he appointed Guide military commissioner, Palace Cavalry and Infantry commander, and Grand Councilor Liu Zhiyuan Ye capital defender, transferred Yanwei to Guide military commissioner, and added concurrent appointment as Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Liu Zhiyuan—Guide military commissioner, commander of the palace horse and foot, and Grand Councilor—was made defender of the Ye capital; Yanwei was shifted to Guide military commissioner and given the concurrent title of Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，徙建立為昭義節度使，進爵韓王；

translations.literal: On guiyou, he transferred Jianli to Zhaoyi military commissioner and advanced his rank to Prince of Han;
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Jianli was moved to Zhaoyi military commissioner and raised to Prince of Han;

sentences.zh: 以建立遼州人，割遼、沁二州隸昭義。

translations.literal: because Jianli was a native of Liao Prefecture, Liao and Qin prefectures were detached and placed under Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: as Jianli came from Liao, the prefectures of Liao and Qin were carved out for Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 徙建雄節度使李德珫為北都留守。

translations.literal: Jianxiong military commissioner Li Deqiu was transferred to be northern capital defender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deqiu, military commissioner of Jianxiong, was reassigned as defender of the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使，同平章事安從進恃其險固，陰蓄異謀，擅邀取湖南貢物，招納亡命，增廣甲卒；

translations.literal: Shannan East Circuit military commissioner and Grand Councilor An Congjin, relying on his rugged stronghold, secretly harbored rebellious designs, on his own authority intercepted Hunan tribute goods, recruited fugitives, and enlarged his armored troops;
translations.idiomatic: An Congjin of Shannan East Circuit, a Grand Councilor, trusted his mountain fastness, nursed secret treason, seized Hunan tribute on his own, gathered outlaws, and swelled his armored ranks;

sentences.zh: 元隨都押牙王令謙、押牙潘知麟諫，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Yuan Sui's chief military adjutant Wang Lingqian and adjutant Pan Zhilin remonstrated; he killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lingqian, chief adjutant at Yuan Sui, and adjutant Pan Zhilin protested; Congjin had them both executed.

sentences.zh: 及王建立徙潞州，帝使問之曰：「朕虛青州以待卿，卿有意則降制。」

translations.literal: When Wang Jianli was transferred to Luzhou, the emperor sent to ask him, saying, "I have left Qingzhou vacant awaiting you; if you are willing, I shall issue the decree."
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Jianli was posted to Luzhou, the emperor sent word: "I have kept Qingzhou open for you. Say the word and I will issue the appointment."

sentences.zh: 從進對曰：「若移青州置漢南，臣即赴鎮。」

translations.literal: Congjin replied, "If Qingzhou were moved south of the Han, your servant would go to his post."
translations.idiomatic: Congjin answered, "Move Qingzhou south of the Han and I will take up the post at once."

sentences.zh: 帝亦不之責。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let the insolence pass without rebuke.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，王延政募敢死士千餘人，夜涉水，潛入潘師逵壘，因風縱火，城上鼓噪以應之，戰棹都頭建安陳誨殺師逵，其眾皆潰。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Wang Yanzheng recruited more than a thousand dare-to-die troops; by night they waded the water, stole into Pan Shikui's camp, and set fire with the wind; the city walls answered with drum and shout; Battle-oar commander Chen Hui of Jian'an killed Shikui, and his forces all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Yanzheng raised over a thousand volunteers who crossed the river by night, slipped into Pan Shikui's camp, and lit fires on the wind while the garrison roared from the walls. Chen Hui of Jian'an, chief of the battle-oars, slew Shikui and the army broke.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，引兵欲攻吳行真寨，建人未涉水，行真及將士棄營走，死者萬人。

translations.literal: On wuyin, he led troops intending to attack Wu Xingzhen's stockade; before the men of Jian had crossed the water, Xingzhen and his officers abandoned the camp and fled, and ten thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he marched on Wu Xingzhen's camp. The Jian troops had not yet reached the ford when Xingzhen and his men fled their lines; ten thousand perished in the rout.

sentences.zh: 延政乘勝取永平、順昌二城。

translations.literal: Yanzheng followed up his victory and took the two cities of Yongping and Shunchang.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the victory, Yanzheng seized Yongping and Shunchang.

sentences.zh: 自是建州之兵始盛。

translations.literal: From this time the troops of Jian Prefecture began to grow strong.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Jian's armies gathered real strength.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，蜀太保兼門下侍郎、同平章事趙季良請與門下侍郎、同平章事毋昭裔，中書侍郎、同平章事張業分判三司，癸卯，蜀主命季良判戶部，昭裔判鹽鐵，業判度支。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Shu Grand Mentor and concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor Zhao Jiliang requested that he, Vice Director and Grand Councilor Wu Zhaoyi, and Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor Zhang Ye divide supervision of the Three Offices; on guimao the Shu ruler ordered Jiliang to oversee the Household Bureau, Zhaoyi salt and iron, and Ye the budget bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, fourth month, Zhao Jiliang of Shu—Grand Mentor, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Grand Councilor—asked to split the Three Offices with Wu Zhaoyi and Zhang Ye. On guimao the Shu ruler put Jiliang over the household accounts, Zhaoyi over salt and iron, and Ye over the budget.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以前橫海節度使馬全節為安遠節度使。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the former Henghai military commissioner Ma Quanjie was made Anyuan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Ma Quanjie, formerly of Henghai, was appointed military commissioner of Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 甲子，吳越孝獻世子弘僔卒。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Hong Pu, filial heir of Xiaoxian of Wuyue, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Hong Pu, heir of Wuyue's Xiaoxian, died.

sentences.zh: 吳越仰仁詮等兵至建州，王延政以福州兵已敗去，奉牛酒犒之，請班師；

translations.literal: When the troops of Wuyue under Yang Renquan and others reached Jian Prefecture, Wang Yanzheng, because the Fuzhou army had already been defeated and withdrawn, presented oxen and wine to feast them and asked them to withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Renquan's Wuyue army reached Jian, Yanzheng—Fuzhou's forces having already been beaten off—brought cattle and wine to entertain them and begged them to march home;

sentences.zh: 仁詮等不從，營於城之西北。

translations.literal: Renquan and the others did not comply and encamped northwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Renquan refused and pitched camp northwest of the walls.

sentences.zh: 延政懼，復遣使乞師於閩王。

translations.literal: Yanzheng grew afraid and again sent envoys to beg troops from the King of Min.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful now, Yanzheng once more pleaded with the King of Min for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 閩王以泉州刺史王繼業為行營都統，將兵二萬救之；

translations.literal: The King of Min appointed Quanzhou prefect Wang Jiye camp commander-in-chief and led twenty thousand troops to rescue him;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Min named Quanzhou prefect Wang Jiye supreme field commander and marched twenty thousand men to his aid;

sentences.zh: 且移書責吳越，遣輕兵絕吳越糧道。

translations.literal: he also sent a letter reproaching Wuyue and dispatched light troops to cut Wuyue's supply lines.
translations.idiomatic: he rebuked Wuyue in writing and sent light forces to sever their grain route.

sentences.zh: 會久雨，吳越軍食盡，五月，延政遣兵出擊，大破之，俘斬以萬計。

translations.literal: As prolonged rain fell, Wuyue's army exhausted its food; in the fifth month Yanzheng sent troops out to strike and routed them greatly, capturing and slaying on the order of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Endless rain emptied Wuyue's stores. In the fifth month Yanzheng counterattacked, shattered them, and killed or captured tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 癸未，仁詮等詮遁。

translations.literal: On guimao, Renquan and the others all fled.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Renquan and his command fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 胡漢筠既違詔命不詣闕，又聞賈仁沼二子欲訴諸朝；

translations.literal: Hu Hanjun, having already defied the imperial edict by not coming to court, also heard that the two sons of Jia Renzhao wished to appeal to the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Hanjun had ignored the summons to court and now learned that Jia Renzhao's two sons meant to petition the throne;

sentences.zh: 及除馬全節鎮安州代李金全，漢筠紿金全曰：「進奏吏遣人倍道來言，朝廷俟公受代，即按賈仁沼死狀，以為必有異圖。」

translations.literal: when Ma Quanjie was appointed to garrison Anzhou in place of Li Jinquan, Hanjun deceived Jinquan, saying, "The memorial gate officer sent a man by double stages to report that the court, once you accept replacement, will investigate the circumstances of Jia Renzhao's death, believing you must harbor some ulterior design."
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Quanjie was named to replace Li Jinquan at Anzhou, Hanjun lied to Jinquan: "A courier from the memorial office rode night and day to say that once you hand over command the court will reopen the inquiry into Jia Renzhao's death—they think you are plotting something."

sentences.zh: 金全大懼。

translations.literal: Jinquan was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan was terrified.

sentences.zh: 漢筠因說金全拒命，自歸於唐；

translations.literal: Hanjun thereupon urged Jinquan to refuse orders and submit himself to Tang;
translations.idiomatic: Hanjun then persuaded Jinquan to defy orders and go over to Tang;

sentences.zh: 金全從之。

translations.literal: Jinquan followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，帝聞金全叛，命馬全節以汴、洛、汝、鄭、單、宋、陳、蔡、曹、濮、申、唐之兵討之，以保大節度使安審暉為之副。

translations.literal: On bingxu, when the emperor heard that Jinquan had rebelled, he ordered Ma Quanjie to campaign against him with troops from Bian, Luo, Ru, Zheng, Shan, Song, Chen, Cai, Cao, Pu, Shen, and Tang, and appointed Baoda military commissioner An Shenhui his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, learning of the revolt, the emperor sent Ma Quanjie against him with armies from Bian, Luo, Ru, Zheng, Shan, Song, Chen, Cai, Cao, Pu, Shen, and Tang, with Baoda military commissioner An Shenhui as second in command.

sentences.zh: 審暉，審琦之兄也。

translations.literal: Shenhui was the elder brother of Shenqi.
translations.idiomatic: Shenhui was Shenqi's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 李金全遣推官張緯奉表請降於唐，唐主遣鄂州屯營使李承裕、段處恭將兵三千逆之。
