translations.literal: Li Jinquan sent his aide Zhang Wei with a memorial requesting surrender to Tang; the Tang ruler sent Ezhou garrison commissioner Li Chengyu and Duan Chugong with three thousand troops to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan sent aide Zhang Wei with a petition of surrender to Tang. The Tang ruler dispatched Li Chengyu and Duan Chugong of the Ezhou garrison with three thousand men to receive him.

sentences.zh: 唐主遣客省使尚全恭如閩，和閩王曦及王延政。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler sent guest-reception commissioner Shang Quangong to Min to reconcile King Xi of Min and Wang Yanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler sent Shang Quangong, guest-reception commissioner, to Min to make peace between King Xi and Wang Yanzheng.

sentences.zh: 六月，延政遣牙將及女奴持誓書及香爐至福州，與曦盟於宣陵。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Yanzheng sent a military adjutant and a female slave bearing the oath text and an incense burner to Fuzhou, and allied with Xi at the Xuan Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yanzheng sent a staff officer and a bondwoman with the covenant and a censer to Fuzhou, where he swore brotherhood with Xi at the Xuan tombs.

sentences.zh: 然兄弟相猜恨猶如故。

translations.literal: Yet the brothers' mutual suspicion and hatred remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Still, the brothers' suspicion and rancor were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，唐李承裕等引兵至安州。

translations.literal: On guimao, Li Chengyu and others of Tang led troops to Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Tang's Li Chengyu and his column reached Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 是夕，李金全將麾下數百人詣唐軍，妓妾資財皆為承裕所奪，承裕入據安州。

translations.literal: That night Li Jinquan led several hundred men of his following to the Tang army; his concubines and goods were all seized by Chengyu, and Chengyu entered and occupied Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That night Jinquan came to the Tang camp with a few hundred retainers. Chengyu seized his women and baggage and took possession of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，馬全節自應山進軍大化鎮，與承裕戰於城南，大破之。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Ma Quanjie advanced from Yingshan to Dahuazhen and fought Chengyu south of the city, routing him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Ma Quanjie marched from Yingshan to Dahuazhen and smashed Chengyu south of the walls.

sentences.zh: 承裕掠安州南走，全節入安州。

translations.literal: Chengyu plundered south of Anzhou and fled; Quanjie entered Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyu looted his way south; Quanjie re-entered Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，安審暉追敗唐兵於黃花谷，段處恭戰死。

translations.literal: On bingwu, An Shenhui pursued and defeated Tang troops at Huanghua Valley; Duan Chugong died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Shenhui ran down the Tang force at Huanghua Valley; Duan Chugong fell fighting.

sentences.zh: 丁未，審暉又敗唐兵於雲夢澤中，虜承裕及其眾。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Shenhui again defeated Tang troops in the Yunmeng marshes and captured Chengyu and his men.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he beat them again in the Yunmeng marshes and took Chengyu and his command prisoner.

sentences.zh: 唐將張建崇據雲夢橋拒戰，審暉乃還。

translations.literal: Tang general Zhang Jianchong held Yunmeng Bridge and resisted; Shenhui then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Tang commander Zhang Jianchong barred the Yunmeng bridge; Shenhui turned back.

sentences.zh: 馬全節斬承裕及其眾千五百人於城下，送監軍杜光業等五百七人於大梁。

translations.literal: Ma Quanjie beheaded Chengyu and fifteen hundred of his men below the walls and sent army overseer Du Guangye and five hundred seven others to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Quanjie executed Chengyu and fifteen hundred followers before the walls and sent overseer Du Guangye and five hundred seven men to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此曹何罪！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What crime have these men committed!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What wrong have these men done!"

sentences.zh: 皆賜馬及器服而歸之。

translations.literal: He bestowed horses, armor, and robes on them all and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: He gave them all horses, arms, and garments and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 初，盧文進之奔吳也，唐主命祖全恩將兵逆之，戒無入安州城，陳於城外。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lu Wenjin had fled to Wu, the Tang ruler ordered Zu Quanen to lead troops to meet him, admonishing that they must not enter Anzhou city but array outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Wenjin first defected to Wu, the Tang ruler had Zu Quanen meet him with orders not to enter Anzhou—camp outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 俟文進出，殿之以歸，無得剽驚。

translations.literal: Wait until Wenjin came out, escort him home in the rear, and do not plunder or alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Wait for Wenjin to emerge, cover his withdrawal, and forbid pillage.

sentences.zh: 及李承裕逆李金全，戒之如全恩；

translations.literal: When Li Chengyu went to meet Li Jinquan, he was admonished as Quanen had been;
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengyu received the same warning when sent to receive Jinquan;

sentences.zh: 承裕貪剽掠，與晉兵戰而敗，失亡四千人。

translations.literal: Chengyu, greedy for plunder, fought the Jin troops and was defeated, losing four thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: but greed for loot drew him into battle with Jin and cost four thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 唐主惋恨累日，自以戒敕之不熟也。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler grieved and resented for many days, blaming himself that his orders had not been made clear enough.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler brooded for days, blaming himself for orders too weakly given.

sentences.zh: 杜光業等至唐，唐主以其違命而敗，不受，復送於淮北，遺帝書曰：「邊校貪功，乘便據壘。」

translations.literal: When Du Guangye and the others reached Tang, the Tang ruler, because they had disobeyed orders and been defeated, would not accept them and sent them back north of the Huai, writing the emperor, "Frontier officers, greedy for merit, seized the chance to occupy the stockade."
translations.idiomatic: When Du Guangye reached Tang, the ruler refused them for disobeying orders and losing the fight, and returned them north of the Huai with a letter: "Border commanders, hungry for glory, took the fort on their own."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「軍法朝章，彼此不可。」

translations.literal: He also wrote, "Military law and court statutes cannot be imposed on one another."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Your military law and our court code cannot govern each other."

sentences.zh: 帝復遣之歸，使者將自桐墟濟淮，唐主遣戰艦拒之，乃還。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent them back; when the envoy was about to cross the Huai from Tongxu, the Tang ruler sent warships to block him, and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor sent them back once more; as the envoy was crossing from Tongxu, Tang warships turned him away.

sentences.zh: 帝悉授唐諸將官，以其士卒為顯義都，命舊將劉康領之。

translations.literal: The emperor invested all the Tang generals with office, made their soldiers the Xianyi Corps, and ordered old commander Liu Kang to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: He commissioned every Tang officer, enrolled the soldiers in the Xianyi Corps, and put veteran Liu Kang in command.

sentences.zh: 巨光曰：違命者，將也，士卒從將之令者也，又何罪乎！

translations.literal: Guang remarked: Those who disobey orders are the generals; the soldiers merely follow the generals' commands—what crime do they have!
translations.idiomatic: Guang observed: Only the generals defy orders; the men only obey—why punish them!

sentences.zh: 受而戮其將以謝敵，吊士卒而撫之，斯可矣，何必棄民以資敵國乎！

translations.literal: Accept them, execute the generals to appease the enemy, console the soldiers and comfort them—that would suffice; why abandon the people to enrich a rival state!
translations.idiomatic: Take them in, kill the commanders to satisfy the foe, mourn and reassure the ranks—that is enough. Why cast subjects away to arm the enemy!

sentences.zh: 唐主使宦者祭廬山，還，勞之曰：「卿此行甚精潔。」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler sent a eunuch to sacrifice at Mount Lu; on his return he comforted him, saying, "Your journey was most pure and austere."
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler sent a eunuch to offer sacrifice at Mount Lu. On his return he praised him: "You kept the rites with admirable purity."

sentences.zh: 宦者曰：「臣自奉詔，蔬食至今。」

translations.literal: The eunuch said, "Since I received the edict I have eaten only vegetables until now."
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch said, "From the day I left court I have eaten nothing but greens."

sentences.zh: 唐主曰：「卿某處市魚為羹，某日市肉為羹，何為蔬食？」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler said, "You bought fish for broth at such-and-such a place and meat for broth on such-and-such a day—why call it eating only vegetables?"
translations.idiomatic: The ruler said, "You bought fish stew here and meat stew there—why claim a vegetarian fast?"

sentences.zh: 宦者慚服。

translations.literal: The eunuch was ashamed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch bowed, abashed.

sentences.zh: 倉吏歲終獻羨餘萬餘石，唐主曰：「出納有數，苟非掊民刻軍，安得羨餘邪！」

translations.literal: At year's end the granary clerks presented a surplus of more than ten thousand piculs; the Tang ruler said, "Receipts and disbursements have fixed numbers—if you are not squeezing the people and cutting the army, how can there be a surplus!"
translations.idiomatic: At year's end clerks offered more than ten thousand piculs of surplus grain. The Tang ruler said, "Accounts are fixed—without robbing the people and shorting the troops, where does surplus come from!"

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，閩主曦城福州西郭以備建人。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, King Xi of Min walled the western outer quarter of Fuzhou against the men of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, seventh month, King Xi of Min fortified Fuzhou's western suburb against Jian.

sentences.zh: 又度民為僧，民避重賦多為僧，凡度萬一千人。

translations.literal: He also ordained commoners as monks; many people, to escape heavy levies, became monks, and in all ten thousand one hundred were ordained.
translations.idiomatic: He also tonsured civilians as monks; to dodge taxes multitudes took the robe—ten thousand one hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，帝賜鄭元弼等帛，遣歸。

translations.literal: On yichou, the emperor bestowed silks on Zheng Yuanbi and others and sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, the emperor gave Zheng Yuanbi and his party silks and dismissed them homeward.

sentences.zh: 李金全之叛也，安州馬步副都指揮使桑千、威和指揮使王萬金、成彥溫不從而死，馬步都指揮使龐守榮誚其愚，以徇金全之意。

translations.literal: When Li Jinquan rebelled, Anzhou deputy horse-and-foot commander Sang Qian, Weihe commander Wang Wanjin, and Cheng Yantong refused to follow and died; horse-and-foot commander Pang Shourong mocked their folly and displayed himself to suit Jinquan's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinquan's revolt, deputy commander Sang Qian, Weihe commander Wang Wanjin, and Cheng Yantong would not join him and died for it; commander Pang Shourong called them fools and curried favor with Jinquan.

sentences.zh: 己巳，詔贈賈仁沼及桑千等官，遣使誅守榮於安州。

translations.literal: On jisi, an edict posthumously honored Jia Renzhao and Sang Qian and others with office and sent an envoy to execute Shourong at Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the court posthumously ennobled Jia Renzhao, Sang Qian, and the rest, and dispatched an agent to kill Shourong at Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 李金全至金陵，唐主待之甚薄。

translations.literal: When Li Jinquan reached Jinling, the Tang ruler treated him very coldly.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinling, the Tang ruler received Jinquan with thin courtesy.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，唐主立齊王璟為太子，兼大元帥，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the Tang ruler installed Prince of Qi Jing as crown prince, concurrently Grand Marshal, and recorder of the Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the Tang ruler named Prince of Qi Jing crown prince, Grand Marshal, and chief of Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 太子太師致仕范延光請歸河陽私第，帝許之。

translations.literal: Retired Grand Mentor Fan Yanguang asked to return to his private residence at Heyang; the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang, retired Grand Mentor, asked leave for his house at Heyang; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 延光重載而行。

translations.literal: Yanguang traveled with a heavy load.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang departed weighed down with treasure.

sentences.zh: 西京留守楊光遠兼領河陽，利其貨，且慮為子孫之患，奏：「延光叛臣，不家汴、洛而就外籓，恐其逃逸入敵國，宜早除之！」

translations.literal: Western Capital defender Yang Guangyuan also held Heyang and coveted his wealth; moreover he feared trouble for his descendants and memorialized, "Yanguang is a rebel minister; instead of dwelling at Bian or Luo he goes to an outer province—I fear he will flee to an enemy state and should be removed early!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan, defender of the western capital, also governed Heyang, coveted the cargo, and feared future trouble. He memorialized: "Yanguang is a traitor. Rather than stay at Bian or Luo he heads for the marches—he may run to the enemy. Cut him down at once!"

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 光遠請敕延光居西京，從之。

translations.literal: Guangyuan requested an edict ordering Yanguang to reside in the western capital; this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan asked that Yanguang be ordered to the western capital; the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 光遠使其子承貴以甲士圍其第，逼令自殺。

translations.literal: Guangyuan had his son Chenggui surround the mansion with armored men and forced him to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan sent his son Chenggui with armored guards to ring the house and demand suicide.

sentences.zh: 延光曰：「天子在上，賜我鐵券，許以不死，爾父子何得如此？」

translations.literal: Yanguang said, "The Son of Heaven is above; he granted me an iron certificate promising I would not die—how dare you father and son do this to me?
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang cried, "The Son of Heaven gave me an iron pledge of life—how dare you and your father do this?

sentences.zh: 己未，承貴以白刃驅延光上馬，至浮梁，擠於河。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Chenggui drove Yanguang onto a horse at naked blades; at the floating bridge he crowded him into the river.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Chenggui forced him onto a horse at sword-point, then at the floating bridge pitched him into the water.

sentences.zh: 光遠奏雲自赴水死，帝知其故，憚光遠之強，不敢詰；

translations.literal: Guangyuan memorialized that he had thrown himself into the water and died; the emperor knew the truth but feared Guangyuan's power and did not inquire;
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan reported a suicide by drowning. The emperor knew better but dared not press so powerful a man;

sentences.zh: 為延光輟朝，贈太師。

translations.literal: he suspended court for Yanguang and posthumously honored him as Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: he mourned Yanguang with court closed and posthumously made him Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 唐齊王璟固辭太子；

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Jing of Tang firmly declined the crown princehood;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Jing of Tang firmly refused the heirship;

sentences.zh: 九月，乙丑，唐主許之，詔中外致箋如太子禮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yichou, the Tang ruler granted it and ordered inner and outer court to address memorials with the etiquette due a crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yichou, the Tang ruler yielded and ordered all memorials to use crown-prince forms.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以翰林學士承旨、戶部侍郎和凝為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Hanlin academician recipient of edicts and Vice Minister of Revenue He Ning was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, He Ning—Hanlin academician recipient of edicts and Vice Minister of Revenue—became Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 己巳，鄴都留守劉知遠入朝。

translations.literal: On jisi, Ye capital defender Liu Zhiyuan came to court.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Liu Zhiyuan, defender of Ye, arrived at court.

sentences.zh: 辛未，李崧奏：「諸州倉糧，於計帳之外所餘頗多。」

translations.literal: On xinwei, Li Song memorialized, "The granaries of the various prefectures retain a considerable surplus beyond the account ledgers."
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Li Song reported, "Prefectural granaries hold far more grain than the ledgers show."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「法外稅民，罪同枉法。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Taxing the people outside the law is a crime equal to perverting the law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Extra-legal levies are as bad as bending the law.

sentences.zh: 倉吏特貸其死，各痛懲之。」

translations.literal: Spare the granary clerks death but punish each of them severely."
translations.idiomatic: Let the clerks live, but flog every one of them hard."

sentences.zh: 翰林學士李澣，輕薄，多酒失，上惡之，丙子，罷翰林學士，並其職於中書舍人，澣，濤之弟也。

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Li Huan was frivolous and often drunk and in error; the emperor disliked him; on bingzi he removed him from Hanlin academician and merged the post into Secretariat drafter; Huan was the younger brother of Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan, a Hanlin academician, was reckless and often drunk on duty. On bingzi the emperor stripped him of Hanlin rank, folded the office into Secretariat drafter, and let him go—Huan was Tao's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠入朝，帝欲徙之它鎮，謂光遠曰：「圍魏之役，卿左右皆有功，尚未之賞，今當各除一州以榮之。」

translations.literal: When Yang Guangyuan came to court, the emperor wished to transfer him to another post and said to Guangyuan, "In the siege of Wei your attendants all had merit, yet they have not been rewarded; now each shall be given a prefecture as honor."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan came to court and the emperor meant to move him elsewhere. He told him, "At the siege of Wei your officers earned reward that never came. I shall give each a prefecture."

sentences.zh: 因以其將校數人為刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed several of his commanders as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: He then named several of Guangyuan's officers prefects.

sentences.zh: 甲申，徙光遠為平盧節度使，進爵東平王。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Guangyuan was transferred to Pinglu military commissioner and advanced to Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Guangyuan was posted to Pinglu military commissioner and made Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁酉，加吳越王元瓘天下兵馬都元帥，尚書令。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingyou, King Yuan Guan of Wuyue was advanced to commander-in-chief of all armies and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, tenth month, on dingyou, Yuan Guan of Wuyue was made commander-in-chief of all armies and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，唐大赦，詔中外奏章無得言「睿」、「聖」，犯者以不敬論。

translations.literal: On renyin, Tang proclaimed a general amnesty and ordered that memorials from within and without must not use the characters "rui" and "sheng"; violators would be judged for disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Tang declared a general amnesty and forbade the characters for "sagely" and "wise" in memorials—disrespect would be punished.

sentences.zh: 術士孫智永以四星聚鬥，分野有災，勸唐主巡東都，乙巳，唐主命齊王璟監國。

translations.literal: Artificer Sun Zhiyong, because four stars gathered in the Dipper and disaster would fall on certain regions, urged the Tang ruler to tour the eastern capital; on yisi the Tang ruler ordered Prince of Qi Jing to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhiyong the diviner, seeing four stars mass in the Dipper and disaster threaten the circuits, urged the Tang ruler east. On yisi the ruler left Prince of Qi Jing as regent.

sentences.zh: 光政副使、太僕少卿陳覺以私憾奏泰州刺史褚仁規貪殘；

translations.literal: Chen Jue, deputy commissioner of the Directorate of Palace Affairs and Vice Minister of the Stud, from private resentment memorialized that Taizhou prefect Chu Rengui was greedy and cruel;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jue, deputy of the palace directorate and Vice Minister of the Stud, bore a private grudge and accused Taizhou prefect Chu Rengui of greed and cruelty;

sentences.zh: 丙午，罷仁規為扈駕都部置，覺始用事。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Rengui was removed and made chief of the imperial escort staff; Jue began to wield power.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Rengui was cashiered to head the imperial escort; from then Jue held the reins.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，唐主發金陵；

translations.literal: On gengxu, the Tang ruler set out from Jinling;
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, the Tang ruler departed Jinling;

sentences.zh: 甲寅，至江都。

translations.literal: On jiayin, he arrived at Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day he reached Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 閩王曦因商人奉表自理；

translations.literal: The Min ruler Xi, through merchants, submitted a memorial explaining himself;
translations.idiomatic: King Xi of Min sent a memorial through merchants pleading his own case;

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲申，以曦為威武節度使，兼中書令，封閩國王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiashen, Xi was made military commissioner of Weiwu, also chief minister of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as king of Min.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiashen day, Xi was appointed Weiwu military commissioner and Secretariat director, and created king of Min.

sentences.zh: 唐主欲遂居江都，以水凍，漕運不給，乃還；

translations.literal: The Tang ruler wished to remain at Jiangdu, but because the water was frozen and grain transport by canal could not be supplied, he returned;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler had wanted to stay at Jiangdu, but ice blocked the waterways and canal supply failed, so he turned back;

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙申，至金陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingchen, he arrived at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingchen day, he reached Jinling.

sentences.zh: 唐右僕射兼門下侍郎、同平章事張延翰卒。

translations.literal: The Tang Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery and co–chief minister Zhang Yanhan died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanhan, the Tang Right Vice Director of State Affairs, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and co–chief minister, died.

sentences.zh: 是歲，漢門下侍郎、同平章事趙損卒；

translations.literal: That year, the Han Vice Director of the Chancellery and co–chief minister Zhao Sun died;
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhao Sun, Han Vice Director of the Chancellery and co–chief minister, died;

sentences.zh: 以寧遠節度使南昌王定保為中書侍郎、同平章事，不逾年亦卒。

translations.literal: Ningyuan military commissioner Wang Dingbao of Nanchang was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and co–chief minister; within the year he too died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dingbao of Nanchang, Ningyuan military commissioner, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and co–chief minister, but died within the year as well.

sentences.zh: 初，帝割雁門之北以賂契丹，由是吐谷渾皆屬契丹，苦其貪虐，思歸中國；

translations.literal: Earlier, the Emperor had ceded the territory north of Yanmen to bribe the Khitan; thereby the Tuyuhun all came under the Khitan, suffered their greed and cruelty, and longed to return to China;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Emperor had surrendered the lands north of Yanmen to buy off the Khitan, and the Tuyuhun thereupon fell under Khitan rule; ground down by their greed and cruelty, they yearned to return to China;

sentences.zh: 成德節度使安重榮復誘之，於是吐谷渾帥部落千餘帳自五台來奔。

translations.literal: Chengde military commissioner An Chongrong again enticed them, and so the Tuyuhun chieftain led more than a thousand households from Wutai to flee and submit.
translations.idiomatic: An Chongrong, military commissioner of Chengde, enticed them again, and a Tuyuhun chief led more than a thousand tents from Wutai to defect.

sentences.zh: 契丹大怒，遣使讓帝以招納叛人。

translations.literal: The Khitan were greatly angered and sent an envoy to reproach the Emperor for receiving rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were furious and sent envoys to rebuke the Emperor for harboring defectors.

sentences.zh: 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝中天福六年（

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, the Sagely, Literary, Martial, Bright, Virtuous, and Filial, in the sixth year of Tianfu of the Middle Kingdom (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu, the Sagely, Literary, Martial, Bright, Virtuous, and Filial, in the sixth year of Tianfu (

sentences.zh: 辛丑，公元九四一年）

translations.literal: xinchou, corresponding to 941 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinchou, corresponding to 941 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙寅，帝遣供奉官張澄將兵二千索吐谷渾在並、鎮、忻、代四州山谷者，逐之使還故土。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on bingyin, the Emperor sent ceremonial attendant Zhang Cheng with two thousand troops to search out Tuyuhun in the valleys of the four prefectures Bing, Zhen, Xin, and Dai and drive them back to their former lands.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on bingyin day, the Emperor sent ceremonial attendant Zhang Cheng with two thousand troops to hunt down Tuyuhun hiding in the mountains of Bing, Zhen, Xin, and Dai and drive them back to their homelands.

sentences.zh: 王延政城建州，週二十里，請於閩王曦，欲以建州為威武軍，自為節度使。

translations.literal: Wang Yanzheng walled Jianzhou, twenty li in circuit, and petitioned the Min ruler Xi to make Jianzhou the Weiwu army and appoint himself its military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzheng fortified Jianzhou with walls twenty li around and asked King Xi of Min to make Jianzhou the Weiwu command and name him its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 曦以威武軍福州也，乃以建州為鎮安軍，以延政為節度使，封富沙王；

translations.literal: Xi said the Weiwu army was at Fuzhou; he therefore made Jianzhou the Zhen'an army, appointed Yanzheng military commissioner, and enfeoffed him as king of Fusha;
translations.idiomatic: Xi replied that Weiwu was based at Fuzhou; he instead made Jianzhou the Zhen'an command, made Yanzheng its military commissioner, and created him king of Fusha;

sentences.zh: 延政改鎮安曰鎮武而稱之。

translations.literal: Yanzheng changed Zhen'an to Zhenwu and used that name.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng renamed Zhen'an to Zhenwu and styled himself accordingly.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬辰，作浮梁於德勝口。

translations.literal: In the second month, on renchen, a pontoon bridge was built at Desheng Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renchen day, a floating bridge was erected at Desheng Ford.

sentences.zh: 彰義節度使張彥澤欲殺其子，掌書記張式素為彥澤所厚，諫止之。

translations.literal: Zhangyi military commissioner Zhang Yanzhe wished to kill his son; chief clerk Zhang Shi, whom Yanzhe had long favored, remonstrated and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanzhe, military commissioner of Zhangyi, meant to kill his son; Zhang Shi, his chief clerk and long-time favorite, admonished him and stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 彥澤怒，射之；

translations.literal: Yanzhe grew angry and shot him;
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhe flew into a rage and shot him;

sentences.zh: 左右素惡式，從而讒之，式懼，謝病去，彥澤遣兵追之，式至邠州，靜難節度使李周以聞，帝以彥澤故，流式商州。

translations.literal: those about him had long hated Shi and joined in slandering him; Shi feared for his life, resigned on grounds of illness and left; Yanzhe sent troops in pursuit; when Shi reached Bin Prefecture, Jingnan military commissioner Li Zhou reported it; because of Yanzhe, the Emperor exiled Shi to Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: his attendants, who had long resented Shi, piled on calumny; Shi, in fear, pleaded illness and departed, but Yanzhe sent soldiers after him; when Shi reached Bin, Li Zhou, military commissioner of Jingnan, reported the matter, and because of Yanzhe the Emperor banished Shi to Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥澤遣行軍司馬鄭元昭詣闕求之，且曰：「彥澤不得張式，恐致不測。」

translations.literal: Yanzhe sent his army marshal Zheng Yuanzhao to the capital to demand him back, saying, "If Yanzhe does not get Zhang Shi back, I fear unforeseen consequences."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhe dispatched army marshal Zheng Yuanzhao to court to demand Shi back, adding, "Unless Yanzhe recovers Zhang Shi, I fear the unpredictable."

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，與之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, having no choice, yielded him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, left no alternative, surrendered him.

sentences.zh: 癸未，式至涇州，彥澤命決口，剖心，斷其四支。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Shi reached Jing Prefecture; Yanzhe ordered his mouth cut open, his heart torn out, and his four limbs severed.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day Shi reached Jingzhou; Yanzhe had his mouth slit, his heart cut out, and his limbs hacked off.

sentences.zh: 涼州軍亂，留後李文謙閉門自焚死。

translations.literal: The Liangzhou garrison mutinied; the acting prefect Li Wenqian shut his gates and burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Liangzhou army mutinied; acting prefect Li Wenqian barred his gates and died by self-immolation.

sentences.zh: 蜀自建國以來，節度使多領禁兵，或以它職留成都，委僚佐知留務，專事聚斂，政事不治，民無所訴。

translations.literal: Since Shu had become a state, military commissioners often commanded palace guards, or remained at Chengdu on other duties and left deputies to manage affairs of record, devoting themselves solely to extortion; government was not administered, and the people had nowhere to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shu had founded its state, military commissioners often held palace guard commands, or stayed in Chengdu on other business while deputies ran local affairs—devoted only to squeezing revenue, neglecting government, and leaving the people without recourse.

sentences.zh: 蜀主知其弊，丙辰，加衛聖馬步都指揮使、武德節度使兼中書令趙廷隱、樞密使、武信節度使、同平章事王處回、捧聖控鶴都指揮使、保寧節度使、同平章事張公鐸檢校官，並罷其節度使。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler knew this abuse; on bingchen he gave honorary titles to Wei Sheng horse-and-foot commander and Wude military commissioner, also chief minister Zhao Tingyin; Privy Council director, Wuxin military commissioner, and co–chief minister Wang Chuhui; and Sacred Crane commander and Baoning military commissioner, co–chief minister Zhang Gongduo—and removed them all from their military commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the abuse, the Shu ruler on bingchen day promoted Zhao Tingyin, Wei Sheng horse-and-foot commander and Wude military commissioner and chief minister; Wang Chuhui, Privy Council director, Wuxin military commissioner, and co–chief minister; and Zhang Gongduo, Sacred Crane commander, Baoning military commissioner, and co–chief minister—to honorary ranks and stripped them of their commands.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲戌，以翰林學士承旨李昊知武德軍，散騎常侍劉英圖知保寧軍，諫議大夫崔鑾知武信軍，給事中謝從志知武泰軍，將作監張言贊知寧江軍。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiaxu, Hanlin academician and chief drafter Li Hao was put in charge of the Wude army; Regular Attendant Liu Yingtu of the Baoning army; Remonstrance and Revision Grandee Cui Luan of the Wuxin army; Supervising Secretary Xie Congzhi of the Wutai army; and Director of Palace Construction Zhang Yanzan of the Ningjiang army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiaxu day, chief Hanlin drafter Li Hao took the Wude command; Regular Attendant Liu Yingtu Baoning; Remonstrance and Revision Grandee Cui Luan Wuxin; Supervising Secretary Xie Congzhi Wutai; and Director of Palace Construction Zhang Yanzan Ningjiang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，閩王曦以其子亞澄同平章事、判六軍諸衛。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Min ruler Xi made his son Yacheng co–chief minister and controller of the Six Armies and various guards.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, King Xi of Min made his son Yacheng co–chief minister and superintendent of the Six Armies and palace guards.

sentences.zh: 曦疑其弟汀州刺史延喜與延政通謀，遣將軍許仁欽以兵三千如汀州，執延喜以歸。

translations.literal: Xi suspected his brother Yanxi, military commissioner of Ting Prefecture, of plotting with Yanzheng; he sent General Xu Renqin with three thousand troops to Ting, seized Yanxi, and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: Xi suspected his brother Yanxi, Tingzhou military commissioner, of colluding with Yanzheng and sent General Xu Renqin with three thousand men to Ting to seize him and bring him back.

sentences.zh: 唐主以陳覺及萬年常夢錫為宣徽副使。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler appointed Chen Jue and Chang Mengxi of Wannian as deputy commissioners of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler made Chen Jue and Chang Mengxi of Wannian deputy commissioners of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，北京留守李德珫遣牙校以吐谷渾酋長白承福入朝。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Beijing acting prefect Li Dechuang sent a military adjutant to escort the Tuyuhun chieftain Bai Chengfu to court.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day Li Dechuang, acting prefect of Beijing, sent a military adjutant to present the Tuyuhun chieftain Bai Chengfu at court.

sentences.zh: 唐主遣通事舍人歐陽遇求假道以通契丹，帝不許。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler sent Communications Officer Ouyang Yu to request passage through Jin territory to reach the Khitan; the Emperor refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler sent Communications Officer Ouyang Yu to ask safe passage through Jin lands to the Khitan; the Emperor denied it.

sentences.zh: 自黃巢犯長安以來，天下血戰數十年，然後諸國各有分土，兵革稍息。

translations.literal: Since Huang Chao's assault on Chang'an, the realm had bled in battle for decades; only then did the various states each hold their allotments of territory, and arms gradually fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: From Huang Chao's sack of Chang'an onward the empire had fought itself bloody for decades; only then did the separate realms settle into their domains and the clatter of arms begin to quiet.

sentences.zh: 及唐主即位，江、淮比年豐稔，兵食有餘，群臣爭言「陛下中興，今北方多難，宜出兵恢復舊疆。」

translations.literal: When the Tang ruler took the throne, the Yangtze and Huai regions had enjoyed successive harvests, with surplus arms and grain; his ministers vied to say, "Your Majesty has restored the dynasty; the north is now full of troubles—you should send troops to recover the old frontiers."
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang ruler's accession the Jiang-Huai country had harvested well year after year, with arms and grain to spare; ministers clamored, "Your Majesty has revived the state; the north is rife with trouble—it is time to march and reclaim the old borders."

sentences.zh: 唐主曰：「吾少長軍旅，見兵之為民害深矣，不忍復言。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler said, "I grew up amid armies and have seen how deeply soldiers harm the people; I cannot bear to hear such talk again.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler replied, "I was raised in the camps and know how ruinous armies are to the people; I will not hear such talk again.

sentences.zh: 使彼民安，則吾民亦安矣，又何求焉！」

translations.literal: If their people are secure, then our people will be secure as well—what more is there to seek!"
translations.idiomatic: If their people are at peace, ours will be at peace too—what else could we want?"

sentences.zh: 漢主遣使如唐，謀共取楚，分其地；

translations.literal: The Han ruler sent envoys to Tang to plot jointly seizing Chu and dividing its territory;
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler sent envoys to Tang to scheme a joint strike on Chu and a partition of its lands;

sentences.zh: 唐主不許。

translations.literal: the Tang ruler refused.
translations.idiomatic: the Tang ruler refused.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使安從進謀反，遣使奉表詣蜀，請出師金、商以為聲援；

translations.literal: Shannan East Circuit military commissioner An Congjin plotted rebellion and sent envoys with a memorial to Shu, asking that troops be sent through Jin and Shang as a supporting demonstration;
translations.idiomatic: An Congjin, military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, plotted rebellion and sent envoys with a memorial to Shu requesting a demonstration through Jin and Shang;

sentences.zh: 丁亥，使者至成都。

translations.literal: on dinghai the envoys reached Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: on dinghai day the envoys reached Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 蜀主與群臣謀之，皆曰：「金、商險遠，少出師則不足制敵，多則漕輓不繼。」

translations.literal: The Shu ruler consulted his ministers; all said, "Jin and Shang are rugged and remote; too few troops would not suffice to control the enemy, and too many would outrun supply by transport."
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler took counsel; all said, "Jin and Shang are steep and far; too small a force could not master the foe, and too large a one could not be fed by transport."

sentences.zh: 蜀主乃辭之。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler therefore declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler therefore declined.

sentences.zh: 又求援於荊南，高從誨遺從進書，諭以禍福；

translations.literal: He also sought aid from Jingnan; Gao Conghui sent Congjin a letter expounding fortune and ruin;
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Jingnan for help; Gao Conghui wrote Congjin, laying out the stakes;

sentences.zh: 從進怒，反誣奏從誨。

translations.literal: Congjin grew angry and in turn lodged a false accusation against Conghui.
translations.idiomatic: Congjin, enraged, lodged a false accusation against Conghui in return.

sentences.zh: 荊南行軍司馬王保義勸從誨具奏其狀，且請發兵助朝廷討之；

translations.literal: Jingnan army marshal Wang Baoyi urged Conghui to report the full facts and also request troops to help the court suppress him;
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan army marshal Wang Baoyi urged Conghui to report everything to the throne and ask to send troops to aid the court;

sentences.zh: 從誨從之。

translations.literal: Conghui followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Conghui agreed.

sentences.zh: 成德節度使安重榮恥臣契丹，見契丹使者，必箕踞慢罵，使過其境，或潛遣人殺之；

translations.literal: Chengde military commissioner An Chongrong was shamed to serve the Khitan; whenever he saw Khitan envoys he would sit sprawled and revile them slowly; when envoys passed through his territory he sometimes secretly sent men to kill them;
translations.idiomatic: An Chongrong of Chengde loathed vassalage to the Khitan; at sight of their envoys he would sprawl insolently and heap abuse on them, and when they crossed his borders he sometimes had them murdered in secret;

sentences.zh: 契丹以讓帝，帝為之遜謝。

translations.literal: the Khitan reproached the Emperor for it, and the Emperor made humble apologies on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: the Khitan reproached the Emperor, who apologized abjectly on Chongrong's behalf.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊午，重榮執契丹使拽剌，遣騎掠幽州南境，軍於博野，上表稱：「吐谷渾、兩突厥、渾、契苾、沙陀各帥部從歸附；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wuwu, Chongrong seized the Khitan envoy Zhuaila, sent horsemen to raid the southern border of You Prefecture, and encamped at Boye; he submitted a memorial stating, "Tuyuhun, the two Türk groups, Hun, Qibi, and Shatuo each lead their tribes in submission;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuwu day Chongrong seized the Khitan envoy Zhuaila, sent cavalry to plunder south of Youzhou, and camped at Boye; his memorial read, "Tuyuhun, the two Türk confederations, Hun, Qibi, and Shatuo have each led their tribes to submit;

sentences.zh: 党項等亦遣使納契丹告身職牒，言為虜所陵暴，又言自二月以來，令各具精甲壯馬，將以上秋南寇，恐天命不佑，與之俱滅，願自備十萬眾，與晉共擊契丹。

translations.literal: the Tangut too have sent envoys surrendering Khitan commission documents, saying they are bullied by the barbarians; they also say that since the second month they have been ordered to ready fine armor and strong horses for a southern raid in the coming autumn—they fear Heaven will not aid them and they will perish together, and wish to ready one hundred thousand men themselves to strike the Khitan jointly with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: the Tangut likewise have sent envoys turning in Khitan appointment papers, complaining of barbarian oppression, and reporting that since the second month they have been ordered to ready stout armor and horses for a southern raid this autumn—they dread Heaven's withdrawal and mutual ruin, and offer to raise one hundred thousand men to join Jin against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 又朔州節度副使趙崇已逐契丹節度使劉山，求歸命朝廷。

translations.literal: Moreover, Shuozhou vice military commissioner Zhao Chong has already expelled Khitan military commissioner Liu Shan and seeks to submit to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Zhao Chong, vice military commissioner of Shuozhou, has driven out Khitan military commissioner Liu Shan and seeks to return to the court's allegiance.

sentences.zh: 臣相繼以聞。

translations.literal: Your servant has reported these matters in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has reported these matters in turn.

sentences.zh: 陛下屢敕臣承奉契丹，勿自起釁端；

translations.literal: Your Majesty has repeatedly charged your servant to obey the Khitan and not provoke trouble on his own;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has repeatedly ordered your servant to serve the Khitan and not pick a quarrel;

sentences.zh: 其如天道人心，難以違拒，機不可失，時不再來。

translations.literal: yet how can Heaven's way and the people's hearts be defied? The moment cannot be missed, and the time will not come again.
translations.idiomatic: yet Heaven's mandate and popular will cannot be refused—the moment will not wait, and the hour will not return.

sentences.zh: 諸節度使沒於虜庭者，皆延頸企踵以待王師，良可哀閔。

translations.literal: The military commissioners lost in the barbarians' court all crane their necks and stand on tiptoe awaiting the royal army—truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders swallowed up in the barbarian court all stretch their necks and stand on tiptoe for the imperial armies—a sight to move pity.

sentences.zh: 願早決計。」

translations.literal: I beg an early decision."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to decide soon."

sentences.zh: 表數千言，大抵斥帝父事契丹，竭中國以媚無厭之虜。

translations.literal: The memorial ran to several thousand characters, broadly denouncing the Emperor for treating the Khitan as a father, exhausting China to flatter insatiable barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ran thousands of words, chiefly rebuking the Emperor for playing the dutiful son to the Khitan and draining China to please insatiable barbarians.

sentences.zh: 又以此意為書遺朝貴及移籓鎮，雲已勒兵，必與契丹決戰。

translations.literal: He also wrote letters in this vein to court nobles and circulated them to the frontier commands, declaring he had already mustered troops and would certainly fight the Khitan to the finish.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote court grandees in the same vein and circulated frontier commands, declaring his forces were already drawn and he would settle accounts with the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 帝以重榮方握強兵，不能制，甚患之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Chongrong now held a strong army and could not be controlled, was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, unable to curb Chongrong while he held a powerful army, was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 時鄴都留守、侍衛馬步都指揮使劉知遠在大梁；

translations.literal: At the time Ye capital acting prefect and Palace Guard horse-and-foot commander Liu Zhiyuan was at Daliang;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Zhiyuan, acting prefect of Ye and Palace Guard horse-and-foot commander, was at Daliang;

sentences.zh: 泰寧節度使桑維翰知重榮已蓄奸謀，又慮朝廷重違其意，密上疏曰：「陛下免於晉陽之難而有天下，皆契丹之功也，不可負之。

translations.literal: Taining military commissioner Sang Weihan knew Chongrong had already harbored treacherous designs and also feared the court would again go against his wishes; he submitted a secret memorial saying, "Your Majesty escaped the peril at Jinyang and gained the realm—all through the Khitan's merit; you must not betray them.
translations.idiomatic: Taining military commissioner Sang Weihan, knowing Chongrong already nursed treason and fearing the court would again indulge him, secretly memorialized, "Your Majesty survived the crisis at Jinyang and won the realm through the Khitan's aid; that debt must not be dishonored.

sentences.zh: 今重榮恃勇輕敵，吐渾假手報仇，皆非國家之利，不可聽也。

translations.literal: Now Chongrong trusts his courage and despises the enemy; the Tuyuhun borrow another's hand for revenge—neither profits the state; do not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong now trusts his valor and scorns the foe; the Tuyuhun use us to settle scores—neither serves the state; do not listen.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀契丹數年以來，士馬精強，吞噬四鄰，戰必勝，攻必取，割中國之土地，收中國之器械；

translations.literal: Your servant has observed that in recent years the Khitan's soldiers and horses have been keen, swallowing the four neighboring states; in battle they always win, in assault they always take; they have carved off China's lands and seized China's weapons;
translations.idiomatic: I have watched the Khitan these several years: their men and horses are sharp, they devour every neighbor, they win every battle and take every siege, carving off Chinese soil and seizing Chinese gear;

sentences.zh: 其君智勇過人，其臣上下輯睦，牛馬蕃息，國無天災，此未可與為敵也。

translations.literal: their ruler surpasses others in wisdom and courage, his ministers are united above and below, cattle and horses multiply, and the state knows no natural disaster—this is not an enemy to be faced.
translations.idiomatic: their khan excels in wit and daring, his ministers are harmonious, their herds thrive, and the realm suffers no natural calamity—this is no foe to meet lightly.

sentences.zh: 且中國新敗，士氣彫沮，以當契丹乘勝之威，其勢相去甚遠。

translations.literal: Moreover China has newly suffered defeat; morale is withered and discouraged; to meet the Khitan's victorious might—the disparity in strength is very great.
translations.idiomatic: China has just been beaten; spirits are crushed; to stand against the Khitan in the flush of victory is to face a gulf in strength.

sentences.zh: 又，和親既絕，則當發兵守塞，兵少則不足以待寇，兵多則饋運無以繼之。

translations.literal: Again, once marriage alliance is broken, troops must be sent to guard the passes; too few cannot await the raiders, and too many cannot be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: And once the marriage tie is severed, armies must guard the passes—too few cannot hold the barbarians, too many cannot be fed.

sentences.zh: 我出則彼歸，我歸則彼至，臣恐禁衛之士疲於奔命，鎮、定之地無復遺民。

translations.literal: When we go out they return; when we return they arrive—I fear the palace guards will weary of rushing about, and Zhen and Ding will have no people left.
translations.idiomatic: We march out and they withdraw; we withdraw and they arrive—I fear the palace guards will be worn out running to and fro, and Zhen and Ding will be stripped of people.

sentences.zh: 今天下粗安，瘡痍未復，府庫虛竭，蒸民困弊，靜而守之，猶懼不濟，其可妄動乎！

translations.literal: Today the realm is barely at peace; the wounds are not yet healed, the treasuries are empty, and the common people are exhausted; merely holding still we still fear we cannot manage it—how can we act rashly!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is only roughly settled; scars are unhealed, coffers empty, and the people spent; even standing pat we may not endure—how dare we stir recklessly!

sentences.zh: 契丹與國家恩義非輕，信誓甚著，彼無間隙而自啟釁端，就使克之，後患愈重；

translations.literal: The Khitan and the state share no light bond of grace and righteousness; their sworn faith is plain; they have given us no opening, yet we would provoke trouble on our own—even if we conquered them, the later trouble would be heavier;
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan and our state are bound by weighty obligation and clear oaths; they have given no opening, yet we would pick a fight—even victory would deepen the aftermath;

sentences.zh: 萬一不克，大事去矣。

translations.literal: if by any chance we did not conquer them, the great enterprise would be lost.
translations.idiomatic: and should we fail, the great cause is lost.

sentences.zh: 議者以歲輸繒帛謂之耗蠹，有所卑遜謂之屈辱，殊不知兵連而不休，禍結而不解，財力將匱，耗蠹孰甚焉！

translations.literal: Critics call the yearly delivery of silks a drain and any show of deference a humiliation, yet they do not see that unending war, knots of disaster never undone, and wealth and strength nearing exhaustion—what drain could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: Men call the annual silk tribute waste and any bowing humiliation, yet they do not see that endless war, troubles never untied, and treasuries running dry—what waste could exceed that!

sentences.zh: 用兵則武吏功臣過求姑息，邊籓遠郡得以驕矜，下陵上替，屈辱孰大焉！

translations.literal: Waging war lets martial officers and meritorious ministers demand excessive indulgence; distant frontier commands grow arrogant; inferiors insult superiors—what humiliation could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: War lets fighting men and meritorious generals demand boundless indulgence, lets distant commands grow proud, and lets the low overturn the high—what humiliation could be greater!

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下訓農習戰，養兵息民，俟國無內憂，民有餘力，然後觀釁而動，則動必有成矣。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to train agriculture and drill for war, nourish troops and give the people rest, wait until the state has no internal worry and the people have surplus strength, and then watch for an opening to act—then action will surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to drill the fields and the ranks, rest the armies and the people, wait until there is no inner trouble and the folk have strength to spare, then strike when the moment shows itself—so every move will succeed.

sentences.zh: 又，鄴都富盛，國家籓屏，今主帥赴闕，軍府無人，臣竊思慢藏誨盜之言，勇夫重閉之義，乞陛下略加巡幸，以杜奸謀。」

translations.literal: Again, Ye capital is rich and strong, the state's screen; now the commander has gone to court and the military headquarters is empty; your servant recalls the saying that indulgence breeds thieves and the brave man double-bars his door—I beg Your Majesty to tour there briefly to forestall treachery."
translations.idiomatic: Again, Ye is wealthy, the realm's shield; its commander is at court and the headquarters empty—I recall the proverb that loose storage invites thieves and the brave man bolts his door; I beg a brief imperial visit to block conspiracy."

sentences.zh: 帝謂使者曰：「朕比日以來，煩懣不決，今見卿奏，如醉醒矣，卿勿以為憂。」

translations.literal: The Emperor told the envoy, "These recent days I have been vexed and unable to decide; now seeing your memorial I am like one waking from drunkenness—do not worry on my account."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told the envoy, "Lately I have been tormented and unable to choose; reading your memorial is like waking from wine—do not fret for me."

sentences.zh: 閩王曦聞王延政以書招泉州刺史王繼業，召繼業還，賜死於郊外，殺其子於泉州。

translations.literal: The Min ruler Xi heard that Wang Yanzheng had written to recruit Quanzhou military commissioner Wang Jiye; he summoned Jiye back, granted death in the suburbs, and killed his son at Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: King Xi of Min learned Wang Yanzheng had written to win over Quanzhou military commissioner Wang Jiye; he recalled Jiye, had him executed outside the walls, and killed Jiye's son at Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，繼業為汀州刺史，司徒兼門下侍郎、同平章事楊沂豐為士曹參軍，與之親善。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jiye was military commissioner of Ting, Grand Master of the Palace and Vice Director of the Chancellery, co–chief minister Yang Yifeng had been his staff officer in the Bureau of Gentlemen and was on intimate terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Jiye governed Ting, Yang Yifeng—Grand Master of the Palace, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and co–chief minister—had served him as a gentlemen's bureau officer and been close to him.

sentences.zh: 或告沂豐與繼業通謀，沂豐方侍宴，即收下獄，明日斬之，夷其族。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Yifeng was in conspiracy with Jiye; Yifeng was just attending a banquet when he was seized and imprisoned; the next day he was beheaded and his clan exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused Yifeng of plotting with Jiye; Yifeng was at a feast when he was seized, jailed, beheaded the next day, and his clan wiped out.

sentences.zh: 沂豐，涉之從弟也，時年八十餘，國人哀之，自是宗族勳舊相繼被誅，人不自保，諫議大夫黃峻舁櫬詣朝堂極諫，曦曰：「老物狂發矣！」

translations.literal: Yifeng was a younger cousin of She and was over eighty; the people mourned him; thereafter kinsmen and old merit-holders were executed in succession, and no one could protect himself; Remonstrance and Revision Grandee Huang Jun shouldered his coffin to the court hall and remonstrated to the limit; Xi said, "The old fool has gone mad!"
translations.idiomatic: Yifeng was She's younger cousin, over eighty; the realm mourned him; from then on kin and old servants of merit were killed one after another until none felt safe; Huang Jun, Remonstrance and Revision Grandee, carried his coffin to the hall and remonstrated to the utmost; Xi said, "The old dotard has lost his wits!"

sentences.zh: 貶漳州司戶。

translations.literal: He was demoted to registrar of Zhang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to registrar of Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 曦淫侈無度，資用不給，謀於國計使國安陳匡范，匡范請日進萬金；

translations.literal: Xi was profligate beyond measure and could not meet his expenses; he consulted National Accounts Commissioner Guo'an Chen Kuangfan, and Kuangfan asked to deliver ten thousand in gold daily;
translations.idiomatic: Xi's extravagance knew no bounds and his funds ran short; he consulted National Accounts Commissioner Chen Kuangfan of Guo'an, who proposed a daily tribute of ten thousand in gold;

sentences.zh: 曦悅，加匡范禮部侍郎，匡范增算商賈數倍。

translations.literal: Xi was pleased, made Kuangfan Vice Minister of Rites, and Kuangfan multiplied merchant levies severalfold.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was delighted, made Kuangfan Vice Minister of Rites, and Kuangfan multiplied merchant taxes several times over.

sentences.zh: 曦宴群臣，舉酒屬匡范曰：「明珠美玉，求之可得；

translations.literal: Xi feasted his ministers and raised his cup to Kuangfan, saying, "Bright pearls and fine jade can be sought and obtained;
translations.idiomatic: At a feast Xi raised his cup to Kuangfan and said, "Pearls and jade may be sought and won;

sentences.zh: 如匡范人中之寶，不可得也。」

translations.literal: a man like Kuangfan is a treasure among men and cannot be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: but a man like Kuangfan is a treasure among men and cannot be found."

sentences.zh: 未幾，商賈之算不能足日進，貸諸省務錢以足之，恐事覺，憂悸而卒，曦祭贈甚厚。

translations.literal: Before long the merchant levies could not meet the daily quota; he borrowed from the various bureau treasuries to make it up; fearing exposure, he died of anxiety; Xi mourned and rewarded him lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon merchant taxes could not meet the daily quota; he borrowed from bureau treasuries to fill the gap; fearing discovery, he died of dread; Xi mourned him with rich rites.

sentences.zh: 諸省務以匡范貸貼聞，曦大怒，斫棺，斷其屍棄水中，以連江人黃紹頗代為國計使。

translations.literal: When the various bureaus reported Kuangfan's loans, Xi was furious, hacked open his coffin, severed the corpse, and cast it into the water; he made Huang Shaopo of Lianjiang the new National Accounts Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the bureaus reported Kuangfan's borrowing, Xi flew into a rage, split the coffin, hacked the corpse apart, and threw it into the river; he replaced him with Huang Shaopo of Lianjiang as National Accounts Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 紹頗請「令欲仕者，自非廕補，皆聽輸錢即授之，以資望高下及州縣房口多寡定其直，自百緡至千緡。」

translations.literal: Shaopo requested, "Let all who wish to take office, unless entering by hereditary privilege, be allowed to pay cash and receive appointment immediately; set the price according to rank and the number of households in prefecture and county, from one hundred to one thousand strings of cash."
translations.idiomatic: Shaopo proposed, "Let anyone who seeks office, except by hereditary privilege, pay cash on the spot for appointment; fix the price by rank and by household count in prefecture and county, from one hundred to one thousand strings."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Xi approved.

sentences.zh: 唐主自以專權取吳，尤忌宰相權重，以右僕射兼中書侍郎、同平章事李建勳執政歲久，欲罷之。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler, because he had seized Wu by concentrating power, especially feared heavy ministerial authority; Right Vice Director of State Affairs, concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat and co–chief minister Li Jianxun had long held power, and he wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler, having seized Wu by hoarding power, especially dreaded powerful ministers; Li Jianxun, Right Vice Director of State Affairs, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and co–chief minister, had governed long, and he wished to oust him.

sentences.zh: 會建勳上疏言事，意其留中，既而唐主下有司施行。

translations.literal: When Jianxun submitted a memorial on affairs, he assumed it would be kept within; instead the Tang ruler had the relevant offices carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianxun memorialized on policy he assumed it would stay within; instead the Tang ruler had the offices implement it.

sentences.zh: 建勳自知事挾愛憎，密取所奏改之；

translations.literal: Jianxun knew the matter carried personal bias; he secretly took back his memorial and altered it;
translations.idiomatic: Jianxun, realizing the matter bore personal favor, secretly retrieved his memorial and altered it;

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊辰，罷建勳歸私第。

translations.literal: in autumn, the seventh month, on wuchen, Jianxun was dismissed and returned to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: in autumn, the seventh month, on wuchen day, Jianxun was dismissed and sent to his private residence.

sentences.zh: 帝憂安重榮跋扈，己巳，以劉知遠為北京留守、河東節度使，復以遼、沁隸河東；

translations.literal: The Emperor, troubled by An Chongrong's arrogance, on jisi made Liu Zhiyuan acting prefect of Beijing and Hedong military commissioner, and again placed Liao and Qin under Hedong;
translations.idiomatic: Worried by An Chongrong's insolence, on jisi day the Emperor made Liu Zhiyuan acting prefect of Beijing and Hedong military commissioner, and again subordinated Liao and Qin to Hedong;

sentences.zh: 以北京留守李德珫為鄴都留守。

translations.literal: Beijing acting prefect Li Dechuang was made acting prefect of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dechuang, acting prefect of Beijing, was made acting prefect of Ye.

sentences.zh: 知遠微時，為晉陽李氏贅婿，嘗牧馬，犯僧田，僧執而笞之。

translations.literal: In his youth Zhiyuan had been a son-in-law of the Li family of Jinyang; he once herded horses and trespassed on a monk's field; the monk seized and flogged him.
translations.idiomatic: In humble days Zhiyuan had married into the Li clan of Jinyang; once while herding horses he trespassed on a monk's field and the monk seized and flogged him.

sentences.zh: 知遠至晉陽，首召其僧，命之坐，慰諭贈遺，眾心大悅。

translations.literal: When Zhiyuan reached Jinyang he first summoned that monk, had him sit, comforted him, and gave gifts; popular sentiment was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Jinyang he first summoned that monk, seated him, soothed him with gifts, and won broad acclaim.

sentences.zh: 吳越府署火，宮室府庫幾盡。

translations.literal: A fire broke out in the Wu-Yue headquarters; palaces and treasuries were nearly all consumed.
translations.idiomatic: Fire broke out in the Wu-Yue headquarters; palaces and treasuries were nearly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 吳越王元瓘驚懼，發狂疾，唐人爭勸唐主乘弊取之，唐主曰：「奈何利人之災！」

translations.literal: The Wu-Yue king Qian Yuanguan was alarmed and terrified and fell into mad illness; Tang men vied to urge the Tang ruler to seize the advantage and take it; the Tang ruler said, "How can we profit from another's disaster!"
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Yuanguan of Wu-Yue was stricken with terror and madness; Tang subjects urged the Tang ruler to strike while they were weak; the Tang ruler said, "How could we profit from another's calamity!"

sentences.zh: 遺使唁之，且賙其乏。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to offer condolences and also relief for their want.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to condole with them and relieve their shortages.

sentences.zh: 閩主曦自稱大閩皇，領威武節度使，與王延政治兵相攻，互有勝負，福、建之間，暴骨如莽。

translations.literal: The Min ruler Xi styled himself emperor of Great Min, held the Weiwu military commission, and waged war against Wang Yanzheng; each had victories, and between Fu and Jian the exposed bones lay thick as brush.
translations.idiomatic: King Xi of Min styled himself emperor of Great Min, kept the Weiwu command, and fought Wang Yanzheng; each won battles, and between Fuzhou and Jianzhou the dead lay thick as scrub.

sentences.zh: 鎮武節度判官晉江潘承祐屢請息兵修好，延政不從。

translations.literal: Zhenwu military commission judge Pan Chengyou of Jinjiang repeatedly asked to cease arms and restore good relations; Yanzheng would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Chengyou of Jinjiang, judge on the Zhenwu staff, repeatedly urged a truce; Yanzheng refused.

sentences.zh: 閩主使者至，延政大陳甲卒以示之，對使者語甚悖慢；

translations.literal: When the Min ruler's envoys arrived, Yanzheng arrayed armored troops in great numbers to display them and addressed the envoys with extreme insolence;
translations.idiomatic: When envoys from the Min court arrived, Yanzheng paraded heavy armor before them and spoke with brazen contempt;

sentences.zh: 承祐長跪切諫，延政怒，顧左右曰：「判官之肉可食乎！」

translations.literal: Chengyou knelt long and remonstrated urgently; Yanzheng grew angry and turned to those about him, saying, "Is the judge's flesh fit to eat!"
translations.idiomatic: Chengyou knelt and remonstrated fiercely; Yanzheng raged and said to his attendants, "Shall we eat the judge's flesh!"

sentences.zh: 承祐不顧，聲色愈厲，閩主曦惡泉州刺史王繼嚴得眾心，罷歸，鴆殺之。

translations.literal: Chengyou paid no heed and grew still sterner in voice and bearing; the Min ruler Xi hated Quanzhou military commissioner Wang Jiyan for winning the people's hearts, recalled him, and killed him with poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyou ignored him and grew only sterner; King Xi of Min hated Quanzhou military commissioner Wang Jiyan for his popular following, recalled him, and poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊子朔，以開封尹鄭王重貴為東京留守。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day wuzi of the month, Kaifeng intendant Prince of Zheng Chonggui was made acting prefect of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the new moon wuzi day, Prince of Zheng Chonggui, Kaifeng intendant, was made acting prefect of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 馮道，李崧屢薦天平節度使兼侍衛親軍馬步副都指揮使、同平章事杜重威之能，以為都指揮使，充隨駕御營使，代劉知遠，知遠由是恨二相，重威所至黷貨，民多逃亡，嘗出過市，謂左右曰：「人言我驅盡百姓，何市人之多也！」

translations.literal: Feng Dao and Li Song repeatedly recommended the ability of Taining military commissioner, also vice commander of the Palace Guard horse and foot and co–chief minister Du Chongwei, to be made chief commander and imperial camp commissioner in place of Liu Zhiyuan; Zhiyuan therefore resented the two chief ministers; wherever Chongwei went he extorted goods and the people fled in numbers; once when he went out through the market he said to those about him, "Men say I have driven off all the common people—why are there so many in the market!"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao and Li Song repeatedly praised Taining military commissioner Du Chongwei—also Palace Guard horse-and-foot vice commander and co–chief minister—as chief commander and imperial camp commissioner, replacing Liu Zhiyuan; Zhiyuan therefore hated both chief ministers; Chongwei plundered wherever he went and the people fled; passing through the market he told his attendants, "They say I have driven away every commoner—why is the market so crowded!"

sentences.zh: 壬辰，帝發大梁。

translations.literal: On renchen, the Emperor set out from Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day the Emperor departed Daliang.

sentences.zh: 己亥，至鄴都。

translations.literal: On jihai, he reached Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day he reached Ye.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，大赦。

translations.literal: On renyin, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 帝以詔諭安重榮曰：「爾身為大臣，家有老母，忿不思難，棄君與親。

translations.literal: The Emperor used an edict to admonish An Chongrong, saying, "You are a great minister with a mother at home; in anger you think not of hardship and abandon your lord and kin.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent an edict to An Chongrong: "You are a great minister with a mother at home; in rage you forget hardship and abandon lord and kin.

sentences.zh: 吾因契丹得天下，爾因吾致富貴，吾不敢忘德，爾乃忘之，何邪？

translations.literal: I gained the realm through the Khitan; you grew rich and noble through me; I dare not forget kindness, yet you forget it—why?
translations.idiomatic: I won the realm through the Khitan; you grew rich through me; I dare not forget that debt, yet you forget yours—why?

sentences.zh: 今吾以天下臣之，爾欲以一鎮抗之，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Now I have made the realm subject to them; you wish to resist them with one command— is that not hard!
translations.idiomatic: Now I have made the realm their vassal; you would resist them with one command—is that not folly!

sentences.zh: 宜審思之，無取後悔！」

translations.literal: Consider carefully and do not bring regret upon yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Think carefully—do not invite regret!"

sentences.zh: 重榮得詔愈驕，聞山南東道節度使安從進有異志，陰遣使與之通謀。

translations.literal: Chongrong grew only more arrogant on receiving the edict; hearing that Shannan East Circuit military commissioner An Congjin harbored rebellious intent, he secretly sent envoys to plot with him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong grew only bolder; learning that An Congjin of Shannan East Circuit nursed rebellion, he secretly opened talks with him.

sentences.zh: 吳越文穆王元瓘寢疾，察內都監章德安忠厚，能斷大事，欲屬以後事，語之曰：「弘佐尚少，當擇宗人長者立之。」

translations.literal: Wu-Yue Literary and Reverent King Qian Yuanguan lay gravely ill; he saw that inner palace commissioner Zhang De'an was loyal and thick and could decide great affairs, and wished to entrust the aftermath to him, telling him, "Hongzuo is still young—you should choose an elder of the clan to establish."
translations.idiomatic: Wu-Yue king Qian Yuanguan lay dying; he judged inner commissioner Zhang De'an loyal and decisive and meant to entrust him with the succession, saying, "Hongzuo is young—choose an elder of the clan to rule."

sentences.zh: 德安曰：「弘佐雖少，群下伏其英敏，願王勿以為念！」

translations.literal: De'an said, "Though Hongzuo is young, the host below submit to his keen intelligence—I beg Your Majesty not to worry on that account!"
translations.idiomatic: De'an replied, "Hongzuo is young, but his officers trust his keen mind—do not trouble yourself!"

sentences.zh: 王曰：「汝善輔之，吾無憂矣。」

translations.literal: The king said, "Aid him well and I shall have no worry."
translations.idiomatic: The king said, "Aid him well and I need not worry."

sentences.zh: 德安，處州人也。

translations.literal: De'an was a man of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: De'an was from Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，元瓘卒。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Yuanguan died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day Yuanguan died.

sentences.zh: 初，內牙指揮使戴惲，為元瓘所親任，悉以軍事委之。

translations.literal: Earlier, inner guard commander Dai Yun had been personally trusted by Yuanguan, who entrusted him with all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dai Yun, inner guard commander, had been Yuanguan's favorite and held all military affairs.

sentences.zh: 元瓘養子弘侑乳母，惲妻之親也，或告惲謀立弘侑。

translations.literal: Yuanguan's adopted son Hongyou's wet nurse was kin to Yun's wife; someone reported that Yun plotted to establish Hongyou.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyou's wet nurse was kin to Yun's wife; someone accused Yun of plotting to make Hongyou king.

sentences.zh: 德安秘不發喪，與諸將謀，伏甲士於幕下；

translations.literal: De'an kept the death secret and consulted the generals, setting armored men in ambush beneath the curtain;
translations.idiomatic: De'an concealed the death, consulted the generals, and hid armored men beneath the curtain;

sentences.zh: 壬子，惲入府，執而殺之，廢弘侑為庶人，複姓孫，幽之明州。

translations.literal: on renzi, Yun entered the headquarters; they seized and killed him, degraded Hongyou to commoner status, restored the surname Sun, and confined him at Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: on renzi day Yun entered headquarters; they seized and killed him, reduced Hongyou to commoner rank, restored the surname Sun, and imprisoned him at Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 是日，將吏以元瓘遺命，承製以鎮海、鎮東副大使弘佐為節度使，時年十四。

translations.literal: That day the generals and officials, by Yuanguan's last command, issued an imperial rescript making Zhenhai and Zhendong vice commissioner Hongzuo military commissioner; he was fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: That day officers, by Yuanguan's last wish, proclaimed Hongzuo—Zhenhai and Zhendong vice commissioner—military commissioner; he was fourteen.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚申，弘佐即王位，命丞相曹仲達攝政。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengshen, Hongzuo took the throne and ordered Chancellor Cao Zhongda to govern as regent.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengshen day, Hongzuo took the throne and made Chancellor Cao Zhongda regent.

sentences.zh: 軍中言賜與不均，舉仗不受，諸將不能制；

translations.literal: In the army men said rewards were unequal; they raised weapons and refused them, and the generals could not control them;
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers complained rewards were unfair, raised weapons and refused them, and the generals could not restrain them;

sentences.zh: 仲達親諭之，皆釋仗而拜。

translations.literal: Zhongda personally exhorted them, and all laid down weapons and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongda exhorted them in person and all laid down arms and bowed.

sentences.zh: 弘佐溫恭，好書，禮士，躬勤政務，發擿奸伏，人不能欺。

translations.literal: Hongzuo was mild and respectful, loved books, honored scholars, personally attended to government, and exposed hidden wrongdoing so that none could deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo was gentle and courteous, loved books, honored scholars, attended government himself, and exposed hidden crimes so none could deceive him.

sentences.zh: 民有獻嘉禾者，弘佐問倉吏：「今蓄積幾何？」

translations.literal: When the people presented auspicious grain, Hongzuo asked the granary officer, "How much is stored now?"
translations.idiomatic: When subjects offered auspicious grain, Hongzuo asked the granary clerk, "How much do we hold?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「十年。」

translations.literal: He answered, "Ten years' worth."
translations.idiomatic: "Ten years' supply," came the answer."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「然則軍食足矣，可以寬吾民」。

translations.literal: The king said, "Then army provisions are enough—we can ease the burden on our people."
translations.idiomatic: The king said, "Then the armies are fed—we can lighten the people's load."

sentences.zh: 乃命復其境內稅三年。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered the realm's taxes remitted for three years.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered taxes within the realm remitted for three years.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，滑州言河決。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Hua Prefecture reported the Yellow River had broken its banks.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day Hua Prefecture reported a breach in the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 帝以安重榮殺契丹使者，恐其犯塞，乙亥，遣安國節度使楊彥詢使於契丹。

translations.literal: Because An Chongrong had killed Khitan envoys, the Emperor feared they would raid the passes; on yihai he sent Anguo military commissioner Yang Yanxun as envoy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Khitan raids after Chongrong killed their envoys, on yihai day the Emperor sent Anguo military commissioner Yang Yanxun to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 彥詢至其帳，契丹主責以使者死狀，彥詢曰：「譬如人家有惡子，父母所不能制，將如之何？」

translations.literal: When Yanxun reached their camp, the Khitan ruler rebuked him for the envoys' deaths; Yanxun said, "It is like a household with a wicked son whom the parents cannot control—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: At the Khitan camp their khan rebuked him for the murdered envoys; Yanxun said, "It is like a wicked son in a household whom parents cannot control—what can they do?"

sentences.zh: 契丹主怒乃解。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler's anger then subsided.
translations.idiomatic: The khan's rage eased.

sentences.zh: 閩主曦以其子琅邪王亞澄為威武節度使、兼中書令，改號長樂王。

translations.literal: The Min ruler Xi made his son Yacheng, king of Langye, Weiwu military commissioner and Secretariat director, and changed his title to king of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: King Xi of Min made his son Yacheng, king of Langye, Weiwu military commissioner and Secretariat director, and retitled him king of Changle.

sentences.zh: 劉知遠遣親將郭威以詔旨說吐谷渾酋長白承福，令去安重榮歸朝廷，許以節鉞。

translations.literal: Liu Zhiyuan sent his close officer Guo Wei with an imperial edict to persuade Tuyuhun chieftain Bai Chengfu to leave An Chongrong and return to the court, promising him a military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiyuan sent his confidant Guo Wei with an edict to persuade Tuyuhun chief Bai Chengfu to abandon An Chongrong for the court, promising a command.

sentences.zh: 威還，謂知遠曰：「虜惟利是嗜，安鐵胡止以袍褲賂之，今欲其來，莫若重賂乃可致耳。」

translations.literal: When Wei returned he told Zhiyuan, "Barbarians care only for profit; An Tiehu merely bribed them with robes and trousers—if you want them to come, nothing but heavy gifts will bring them."
translations.idiomatic: Wei returned and told Zhiyuan, "Barbarians follow profit alone; An Iron Hu only bought them with robes—heavy gifts alone will draw them."

sentences.zh: 知遠從之，且使謂承福曰：「朝廷已割爾曹隸契丹，爾曹當自安部落；

translations.literal: Zhiyuan followed his advice and also had him tell Chengfu, "The court has already cut you off from the Khitan; you should settle your tribes in peace;
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan agreed and had Wei tell Chengfu, "The court has severed you from the Khitan; keep your tribes in peace;

sentences.zh: 今乃南來助安重榮為逆，重榮已為天下所棄，朝夕敗亡。

translations.literal: yet now you come south to aid An Chongrong in rebellion; Chongrong is already abandoned by the realm and will fail within days.
translations.idiomatic: yet you march south for An Chongrong's rebellion; the realm has abandoned him and he will fall any day.

sentences.zh: 爾曹宜早從化，勿俟臨之以兵，南北無歸，悔無及矣。」

translations.literal: You should submit early; do not wait until armies come upon you with nowhere to turn north or south—then regret will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Submit early; do not wait for armies when you have nowhere to flee north or south—regret will be too late."

sentences.zh: 承福懼，冬，十月，帥其眾歸於知遠。

translations.literal: Chengfu was afraid; in winter, the tenth month, he led his people to submit to Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chengfu feared; in winter, the tenth month, he led his people to Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 知遠處之太原東山及嵐、石之間，表承福領大同節度使，收其精騎以隸麾下。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan settled them between the eastern hills of Taiyuan and Lan and Shi, memorialized that Chengfu should hold the Datong military commission, and took his picked horsemen into his own command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan settled them on Taiyuan's eastern hills and between Lan and Shi, had Chengfu named Datong military commissioner, and enrolled his best horsemen.

sentences.zh: 始，安重榮稱檄諸道，雲與吐谷渾、達靼，契苾同起兵，既而承福降知遠，達靼、契苾亦莫之赴，重榮勢大沮。

translations.literal: Earlier, when An Chongrong issued proclamations to the circuits claiming he would rise with the Tuyuhun, Tatars, and Qibi, Chengfu then submitted to Zhiyuan and the Tatars and Qibi also did not come; Chongrong's strength was greatly broken.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongrong had proclaimed joint rebellion with Tuyuhun, Tatars, and Qibi, Chengfu defected and the Tatars and Qibi stayed away; Chongrong's cause collapsed.

sentences.zh: 閩主曦即皇帝位。

translations.literal: The Min ruler Xi assumed the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: King Xi of Min took the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 王延政自稱兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: Wang Yanzheng styled himself commander-in-chief of armies and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzheng styled himself commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 閩同平章事李敏卒。

translations.literal: Min co–chief minister Li Min died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Min, Min co–chief minister, died.

sentences.zh: 帝之發大梁也，和凝請曰：「車駕已行，安從進若反，何以備之？」

translations.literal: As the Emperor was leaving Daliang, He Ning requested, "The imperial carriage has already departed—if An Congjin rebels, how shall we meet it?"
translations.idiomatic: As the Emperor left Daliang, He Ning asked, "The court is on the road—if An Congjin rebels, how do we answer?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿意如何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "What is your thought?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "What do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 凝請密留空名宣敕十數通，付留守鄭王，聞變則書諸將名，遣擊之；

translations.literal: Ning asked to keep secretly ten-odd blank edicts with the acting prefect Prince of Zheng; on trouble he would fill in generals' names and dispatch them to strike;
translations.idiomatic: Ning asked to leave a dozen blank edicts with acting prefect Prince of Zheng to fill in generals' names and dispatch them on alarm;

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: the Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，從進舉兵攻鄧州，唐州刺史武延翰以聞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Congjin raised troops and attacked Deng Prefecture; Tang Prefecture military commissioner Wu Yanhan reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Congjin attacked Dengzhou; Tangzhou military commissioner Wu Yanhan reported it.

sentences.zh: 鄭王遣宣徽南院使張從恩、武德使焦繼勳、護聖都指揮使郭金海、作坊使陳思讓將大梁兵就申州刺史李建崇兵於葉縣以討之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zheng sent Southern Palace Secretariat deputy Zhang Cong'en, Wude commissioner Jiao Jixun, Sacred Guard commander Guo Jinhai, and workshop commissioner Chen Siyang with Daliang troops to join Shen Prefecture military commissioner Li Jianchong's men at Ye County to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zheng sent Zhang Cong'en, Jiao Jixun, Guo Jinhai, and Chen Siyang with Daliang troops to join Li Jianchong of Shenzhou at Ye County.

sentences.zh: 金海，本突厥；

translations.literal: Jinhai was originally a Türk;
translations.idiomatic: Jinhai was a Türk by birth;

sentences.zh: 思讓，幽州人也。

translations.literal: Siyang was a man of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Siyang was from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以西京留守高行周為南面軍前都部署，前同州節度使宋彥筠副之，張從恩監焉；

translations.literal: On dingchou, western capital acting prefect Gao Xingzhou was made overall commander of the southern campaign, former Tong Prefecture military commissioner Song Yanyun his deputy, with Zhang Cong'en as overseer;
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day Gao Xingzhou, western capital acting prefect, was made southern campaign commander, former Tongzhou military commissioner Song Yanyun his deputy, Zhang Cong'en overseer;

sentences.zh: 又以郭金海為先鋒使，陳思讓監焉。

translations.literal: Guo Jinhai was also made vanguard commander, with Chen Siyang as overseer.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jinhai was made vanguard, Chen Siyang overseer.

sentences.zh: 彥筠，滑州人也。

translations.literal: Yanyun was a man of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyun was from Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以鄴都留守李德珫權東京留守，召鄭王重貴如鄴都。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Ye acting prefect Li Dechuang was made acting eastern capital prefect in his stead, and Prince of Zheng Chonggui was summoned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Li Dechuang was made acting eastern capital prefect while Chonggui was summoned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 安從進攻鄧州，威勝節度使安審暉據牙城拒之，從進不能克而退。

translations.literal: An Congjin attacked Deng Prefecture; Weisheng military commissioner An Shenhui held the headquarters city against him, and Congjin could not take it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Congjin attacked Dengzhou; Weisheng military commissioner An Shenhui held the walled headquarters and Congjin withdrew unbeaten.

sentences.zh: 癸未，從進至花山，遇張從恩兵，不意其至之速，合戰，大敗，從恩獲其子牙內都指揮使弘義，從進以數十騎奔還襄州，嬰城自守。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Congjin reached Flower Mountain and met Zhang Cong'en's army; not expecting them so soon, they joined battle and he was utterly defeated; Cong'en captured his son, inner guard commander Hongyi; Congjin fled back to Xiang Prefecture with several dozen horsemen and shut the city to hold out.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day Congjin reached Flower Mountain, met Zhang Cong'en unexpectedly, was routed, and lost his son Hongyi; Congjin fled to Xiangzhou with a few dozen horsemen and barred the gates.

sentences.zh: 唐主性節儉，常躡蒲屨，盥□用鐵盎，暑則寢於青葛帷，左右使令惟老醜宮人，服飾粗略。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler was frugal by nature; he often wore rush sandals, used an iron basin for washing, in summer slept within green vine curtains, and had only old and homely palace women wait on him, with plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler was frugal by nature: rush sandals, an iron basin for ablutions, summer sleep under green vine curtains, only old and plain palace women in attendance, dress unadorned.

sentences.zh: 死國事者雖士卒皆給祿三年。

translations.literal: Even common soldiers who died for the state were granted three years' salary.
translations.idiomatic: Even common soldiers who died for the state received three years' stipend.

sentences.zh: 分遣使者按行民田，以肥瘠定其稅，民間稱其平允。
