translations.literal: He dispatched envoys to inspect the people's fields and set tax according to fertility and barrenness; the people praised the fairness.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to survey fields and set tax by soil quality; the people called it fair.

sentences.zh: 自是江、淮調兵興役及它賦斂，皆以稅錢為率，至今用之。

translations.literal: Thereafter levies for troops, corvée, and other exactions in the Jiang-Huai all used tax money as the standard—a practice used to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Jiang-Huai levies for troops, corvée, and other dues were reckoned in tax coin—a practice that endures.

sentences.zh: 唐主勤於聽政，以夜繼晝，還自江都，不復宴樂；

translations.literal: The Tang ruler was diligent in hearing government, continuing day into night; returning from Jiangdu he no longer held feasts;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler worked government day into night; after Jiangdu he gave up feasting;

sentences.zh: 頗傷躁急，內侍王紹顏上書，以為「今春以來，群臣獲罪者眾，中外疑懼。」

translations.literal: he was somewhat hurt by irritability; inner attendant Wang Shaoyan submitted a memorial saying, "Since this spring many ministers have been punished; within and without there is suspicion and fear."
translations.idiomatic: irritability wounded him; attendant Wang Shaoyan memorialized that since spring many ministers had been punished and court and country were uneasy."

sentences.zh: 唐主手詔釋其所以然，令紹顏告諭中外。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler wrote a hand edict explaining why, and had Shaoyan announce it within and without.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler wrote a hand edict explaining himself and had Shaoyan proclaim it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙戌朔，徙鄭王重貴為齊王，充鄴都留守；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day bingxu of the month, Prince of Zheng Chonggui was moved to Prince of Qi and made Ye acting prefect;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the new moon bingxu day, Prince of Zheng Chonggui became Prince of Qi and Ye acting prefect;

sentences.zh: 以李德珫為東都留守。

translations.literal: Li Dechuang was made eastern capital acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dechuang was made eastern capital acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以高行周知襄州行府事。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Gao Xingzhou was put in charge of Xiang Prefecture's provisional headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Gao Xingzhou was put in charge of affairs at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔荊南、湖南共討襄州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jingnan and Hunan jointly to attack Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Jingnan and Hunan to attack Xiangzhou jointly.

sentences.zh: 高從誨遣都指揮使李端將水軍數千至南津，楚王希範遣天策都軍使張少敵將戰艦百五十艘入漢江助行周，仍各運糧以饋之。

translations.literal: Gao Conghui sent chief commander Li Duan with several thousand naval troops to Nanjin; Chu king Xifan sent Celestial Strategy army commander Zhang Shaodi with a hundred fifty warships into the Han to aid Xingzhou, each also shipping grain to feed them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Conghui sent Li Duan with thousands of sailors to Nanjin; Chu king Xifan sent Zhang Shaodi with a hundred fifty warships up the Han to aid Xingzhou, each shipping grain.

sentences.zh: 少敵，佶之子也。

translations.literal: Shaodi was Ji's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shaodi was the son of Ji.

sentences.zh: 安重榮聞安從進舉兵反，謀遂決，大集境內饑民，眾至數萬，南向鄴都，聲言不朝。

translations.literal: An Chongrong, hearing that An Congjin had rebelled, settled on his plan, gathered starving people throughout his territory until they numbered tens of thousands, and marched south on Ye, declaring he would not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Congjin had rebelled, Chongrong mustered tens of thousands of hungry men and marched south on Ye, vowing never to attend court again.

sentences.zh: 初，重榮與深州人趙彥之俱為散指揮使，相得歡甚。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chongrong and Zhao Yanzhi of Shen Prefecture had both been irregular commanders and were on terms of great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong and Zhao Yanzhi of Shenzhou had once been irregular commanders and were close friends.

sentences.zh: 重榮鎮成德，彥之自關西歸之，重榮待遇甚厚，使彥之招募黨眾；

translations.literal: When Chongrong governed Chengde, Yanzhi returned to him from Guanxi; Chongrong treated him very generously and had him recruit partisans;
translations.idiomatic: When Chongrong took Chengde, Yanzhi came from the west; Chongrong favored him richly and had him recruit followers;

sentences.zh: 然心實忌之，及舉兵，止用為排陳使，彥之恨之。

translations.literal: yet in his heart he truly envied him, and when he raised troops he only made him battle-array commander; Yanzhi resented this.
translations.idiomatic: yet he secretly envied him and, on rebellion, made him only battle-array commander; Yanzhi hated it.

sentences.zh: 帝聞重榮反，壬辰，遣護聖等馬步三十九指揮擊之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, hearing Chongrong had rebelled, on renchen sent thirty-nine horse-and-foot commands of the Sacred Guard and others to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the rebellion, on renchen day the Emperor sent thirty-nine Sacred Guard horse-and-foot commands against him.

sentences.zh: 以天平節度使杜重威為招討使，安國節度使馬全節副之，前永清節度使王周為馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: Taining military commissioner Du Chongwei was made suppression commissioner, Anguo military commissioner Ma Quanjie his deputy, and former Yongqing military commissioner Wang Zhou horse-and-foot chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei of Taining was suppression commissioner, Ma Quanjie of Anguo his deputy, and former Yongqing military commissioner Wang Zhou chief adjutant.

sentences.zh: 安從進遣其弟從貴將兵逆均州刺史蔡行遇，焦繼勳邀擊，敗之，獲從貴，斷其足而歸之。

translations.literal: An Congjin sent his brother Conggui with troops to intercept Jun Prefecture military commissioner Cai Xingyu; Jiao Jixun intercepted and defeated him, captured Conggui, severed his feet, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Congjin sent his brother Conggui against Junzhou military commissioner Cai Xingyu; Jiao Jixun intercepted, defeated him, captured Conggui, severed his feet, and returned him.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，杜重威與安重榮遇於宗城西南，重榮為偃月陳，官軍再擊之，不動；

translations.literal: On wuxu, Du Chongwei met An Chongrong southwest of Zong City; Chongrong formed a crescent array; the government army attacked twice and could not move them;
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day Du Chongwei met Chongrong southwest of Zongcheng; Chongrong formed a crescent line; government troops attacked twice without shifting them;

sentences.zh: 重威懼，欲退。

translations.literal: Chongwei feared and wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei feared and meant to retreat.

sentences.zh: 指揮使宛丘王重胤曰：「兵家忌退。

translations.literal: Commander Wang Chongyin of Wankiu said, "In warfare withdrawal is taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wang Chongyin of Wankiu said, "Armies must not retreat.

sentences.zh: 鎮之精兵盡在中軍，請公分銳士擊其左右翼，重胤為公以契丹直衝其中軍，彼必狼狽。」

translations.literal: The command's elite troops are all in the center—please divide sharp troops to strike their left and right wings; Chongyin will charge the center with Khitan horse for you, and they will surely be thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Chengde's best troops are in the center—split your shock troops against both wings; I will charge the center with Khitan horse and break them.

sentences.zh: 重威從之。

translations.literal: Chongwei followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei agreed.

sentences.zh: 鎮人陳稍卻，趙彥之卷旗策馬來降。

translations.literal: The Chengde men gave way slightly; Zhao Yanzhi furled his banner and spurred his horse to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chengde lines bent; Zhao Yanzhi furling his banner galloped over to surrender.

sentences.zh: 彥之以銀飾鎧冑及鞍勒，官軍殺而分之。

translations.literal: Yanzhi's armor and saddle were ornamented with silver; the government army killed him and divided the spoils.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi wore silver-trimmed armor and harness; government troops killed him and divided the plunder.

sentences.zh: 重榮聞彥之叛，大懼，退匿於輜重中，官軍從而乘之，鎮人大潰，斬首萬五千級。

translations.literal: Chongrong, hearing Yanzhi had defected, was greatly afraid, withdrew and hid among the baggage train; the government army pressed after them; the Chengde men broke utterly, and fifteen thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Yanzhi had turned, Chongrong hid among the wagons; government troops pressed the rout and took fifteen thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 重榮收餘眾，走保宗城，官軍進攻，夜分，拔之。

translations.literal: Chongrong gathered the remnant, fled to hold Zong City, and the government army advanced to attack; in the night watch they took it.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong rallied survivors, fled into Zongcheng, and government troops stormed it in the night watch.

sentences.zh: 重榮以十餘騎走還鎮州，嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Chongrong fled back to Zhen Prefecture with a little over ten horsemen and shut the city to hold out.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong fled to Zhenzhou with a dozen horsemen and barred the gates.

sentences.zh: 會天寒，鎮人戰及凍死者二萬餘人。

translations.literal: It happened to be bitter cold; of the Chengde men more than twenty thousand died in battle and from freezing.
translations.idiomatic: The cold was fierce; twenty thousand Chengde men fell in battle or froze.

sentences.zh: 契丹聞重榮反，乃聽楊彥詢還。

translations.literal: The Khitan, hearing Chongrong had rebelled, then allowed Yang Yanxun to return.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the rebellion, the Khitan let Yang Yanxun return.

sentences.zh: 庚子，冀州刺史張建武等取趙州。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Ji Prefecture military commissioner Zhang Jianwu and others took Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Zhang Jianwu of Jizhou and others took Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 漢主寢疾，有胡僧謂漢主名龔不利；

translations.literal: The Han ruler lay gravely ill; a foreign monk said the Han ruler's name Gong was unlucky;
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler lay dying; a foreign monk said the name Gong was ill-omened;

sentences.zh: 漢主自造「龑」字名之，義取「飛龍在天」，讀若儼。

translations.literal: the Han ruler invented a new character (combining "dragon" and "yan") for his name, taking the sense "dragon flying in heaven," pronounced like yan.
translations.idiomatic: the Han ruler invented a new character (combining "dragon" and "yan") for his name, taking the sense "dragon flying in heaven," pronounced like yan.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，制以錢弘佐為鎮海、鎮東軍節度使兼中書令、吳越國王。

translations.literal: On gengxu, an edict made Qian Hongzuo Zhenhai and Zhendong military commissioner, also Secretariat director, and king of Wu-Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day an edict made Qian Hongzuo Zhenhai and Zhendong military commissioner, Secretariat director, and king of Wu-Yue.
